articleTitle: Intelligent Global Sliding Mode Control of Anti-Lock Braking System Using Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article provides an overview of optimization algorithms for gain tuning in sliding mode control applied to the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). Anti-Lock Braking is crucial for ensuring vehicle safety, and a significant challenge lies in selecting accurate control gains to ensure system stability and rapid convergence to the desired target. Initially, we introduce a global sliding mode control approach for ABS and establish its asymptotic stability using the Lyapunov method. Subsequently, to enhance convergence, we propose two algorithms designed to select optimal sliding mode control gains, aiming to minimize the error between the actual wheel slip ratio and the desired value. Through design and simulation phases, our study demonstrates the effectiveness of these algorithms in achieving stable and rapid convergence of the output signal to the desired target. We then conduct a comparative analysis of the two proposed tuning algorithms based on convergence delay time and error tracking rate.

articleTitle: Effects of applying stemmers with word representation on Arabic text classification performance using deep learning methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Due to the increasing of using the Arabic language on the internet in the last decade, it became necessary to create an automated Arabic text classification model to manage this huge number of generated texts. Many studies have investigated the ap-plications of Natural Language pre-processing (NLP) techniques in Arabic text processing. This includes stemming, word represen-tation, and the creation of classifier models. Where all contribute to improving Arabic language pre-processing and understanding. In this work, we studied the effect of different stemming methods with word representations on Arabic text classification using RNNs models. We made this study by comparing the accuracy of different combinations of stemmers aproches (without, root-based, and light-based stemming), word representation (Word2Vec, FastText, and GloVe), and four Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) architectures which are: LSTM, Bi-LSTM, GRU, and Bi-GRU. The best results in the terms of accuracy was achived by using the combination of no stemming with Word2Vec as a word representation and Bi-GRU as a classifier.

articleTitle: Ansys material designer modeling of earthen straw bio-composite material for the mechanical behavior prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Modeling and simulation are powerful tools which have shown their benefits in several sectors by allowing the prediction and/or the understanding of the behavior of objects in the conception phase or already existing. In this paper, construction industry was explored by carrying out 3D modeling of the earthen-straw composite material in order to predict its mechanical properties through ANSYS Material Designer. Hence, this bio-composite material has been modeled as a randomly distributed Short Fibers Reinforced Composite (SFRC) with a random geometry of fibers. Then, the dimensions of the brick were varied in order to study the effect of the brick size on the effective properties of this material. It was concluded that the size of the brick does not influence its mechanical behavior. Thus, the Representative Elementary Volume (REV) of the raw earth brick has been chosen. On the other hand, the effect of fiber volume fraction (Vf) on the elastic properties of this bio-composite material was investigated for the straw contents from 5% to 25% by volume of earthen. It shows that the addition of straw fibers in the earthen matrix with elasticity equal to 2000 MPa has improved its mechanical resistance. Indeed, for 25% of straw fiber's filling rate, we have found 2348 MPa in the young's modulus of the earthen straw composite material, which is equivalent to an increase of 17.4% in this intrinsic parameter. The model was finally validated by its comparison to some well-known analytical model's prediction. The results of ANSYS material designer simulation demonstrate a high level of accuracy compared to analytical methods.

articleTitle: Smart Agriculture for Sustainability: The Implementation of Smart Irrigation Using Real-Time Embedded System Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Faced with the growing challenges of water management in agriculture, this paper explores the shortcomings of traditional irrigation methods and calls for the adoption of innovative technologies to meet these challenges. This paper proposed an innovative solution by combining embedded systems (Controllers) and environmental sensors to create a real-time intelligent irrigation system. Based on these technologies, the system automatically adjusts irrigation operations in real-time, according to environmental conditions, thus improving water use efficiency. Essentially, this study developed an intelligent system capable of dynamically adjusting irrigation based on environmental parameters, including soil moisture and water level thresholds. This approach aims to reduce water wastage while improving agricultural productivity. The methodology involves the use of an Arduino Mega 2560 microcontroller, and advanced sensors such as temperature, humidity (DHT22), moisture, water level, and pumps as actuators. The algorithm developed enabled continuous monitoring and adaptive control of the pump, as well as data logging on the controller for real-time feedback. Tests carried out confirm the effectiveness of the smart irrigation system since it has considerably reduced water wastage while maintaining optimum agricultural productivity, compared with traditional methods. This innovative approach enables farmers to save considerable quantities of water while guaranteeing a high-quality harvest. By encouraging more sustainable farming practices, this solution contributes to the preservation of natural resources and the long-term sustainability of agriculture.

articleTitle: Arabic Multiclass Emotional Analysis Using a Bidirectional GRU-LSTM Deep Model on Twitter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Recognizing emotional states within Arabic tweets is a challenging task due to the inherent complexity of the Arabic language. This complexity encompasses aspects such as ambiguity, agglutination, dialectal variations, and morphological richness. Additionally, user-generated data frequently include misspelled words, abbreviations, acronyms, slang, informal language, and non-standard punctuation, further complicating the task. In our research, we have implemented an efficient multiclass emotional recognition classifier. To achieve this, we proposed a Bidirectional GRU-LSTM deep learning model. This model is designed to capture high-quality global features within the input tweet. Our experimental evaluation, conducted using a benchmark dataset, has produced highly promising results and significant performance improvements.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Crisis Management a Systematic Literature Review using PRISMA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research presents the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on crisis and risk management in the industrial sector, offering an international view. We examine how AI can improve industries' preparedness and responsiveness to unforeseen challenges. Using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews (PRISMA) standards, our systematic review compiled data from research conducted between 2019 and 2023, mainly sourced from the Web of Science and Scopus databases. The analysis, which encompasses 66 articles, reveals a notable concentration of research worldwide. A major challenge identified is the alignment of AI capabilities with the specific crisis management requirements of industries. The results suggest that the advancement of AI is essential for developing innovative strategies in Industry 4.0 and highlight the importance of AI innovation and collaborative practices in strengthening industrial resilience to crises. The aim is to explore how integrating AI into industrial strategies can not only prevent risks but also improve crisis management.

articleTitle: Integrated Control and Energy Flow Management in Hybrid Stand-Alone Photovoltaic/Wind Systems with Battery Storage Using Fuzzy Logic Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper addresses the control and management of an energy conversion system within a stand-alone microgrid, comprising various renewable energy sources, DC/DC, DC/AC converters and a storage system. Different control objectives are defined, such as energy availability, load demand, and storage system state of charge. To meet these scenarios, an energy flow management system is developed in this work. The primary roles of this management algorithm are to ensure the safety of all microgrid components, increase the lifetime of the storage system, and improve energy efficiency. To achieve these objectives, multiple control loops are designed based on fuzzy logic controllers to guarantee appropriate system operating modes. The effectiveness of this control and energy management strategy is evaluated using the MATLAB/Simulink/Simpower environment, demonstrating its ability to achieve the specified objectives.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation on the Charging Process of Phase Change Materials (PCM) in Thermal Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study introduces an advanced simulation model that highlights the importance of using phase change materials (PCMs) for thermal energy storage in the pursuit of sustainable energy solutions. The model specifically examines the dynamics of heat transfer oil (HTO), more specifically therminol VP-l, as it moves through a coil within a PCM storage medium using RT28. These choices represent a strategic selection of materials aimed at maximizing energy storage and transmission in situations with varying demand. The simulation accurately computes various crucial parameters that are essential for assessing the efficiency of thermal storage systems based on PCMs. These encompass meticulous energy balances, offering a comprehensive perspective on energy preservation and effectiveness within the system. The model also evaluates the thermal efficiency, measuring the effectiveness of therminol VP-1 in transferring heat to the PCM RT28. Furthermore, the model excels at measuring ambient losses, a crucial factor in assessing the overall efficiency of the system. It accurately calculates the temperature at the outlet on the hot side, which is a critical measure of the efficiency of heat transfer in the system under different operating conditions. Moreover, the simulation provides a comprehensive examination of the storage temperature in the PCM, which is crucial for optimizing the medium's ability to retain thermal energy. This simulation model is an essential tool for improving our comprehension of PCM-based energy storage systems. It specifically emphasizes the significance of therminol VP-l and PCM RT28 in enhancing the design and efficiency of sustainable thermal energy solutions.

articleTitle: Output Feedback Control of a WPT Charger based on Sliding Mode and High Gain Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper focuses on the regulation of the output voltage of a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) charger feeding an Electric Vehicle (EV) battery through an On-Board Charger (OBC) with a DC input voltage. To achieve optimal OBC performance, maintaining a well-regulated voltage is crucial. However, direct control of the WPT charger's output voltage is challenging due to the non-minimum phase nature of the WPT circuit. To address this, the paper proposes an indirect control technique where the output voltage is regulated by controlling the current in the ground side coil. After establishing an accurate model of the WPT charger, a nonlinear controller has been designed using the sliding mode control technique. Although effective in simulation scenarios, the main limitation of the controller is the need to measure all signals involved, increasing cost and complexity. To overcome this, a high-gain observer is introduced, requiring only two measured signals. This reduces the complexity and cost of the proposed control technique while maintaining effectiveness, as validated through simulation scenarios.

articleTitle: Accessing the Students’ Perception Towards Cloud Computing Applications in Their Learning Process in Higher Education Institutions: Role of Trust and Security in Technology Acceptance Using Smart Education
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The study aims to find the factors that influence the perception of students of higher education institutions in Punjab towards the use of Cloud Computing Applications in their learning environment. The objective of the study includes: (a) Role of Trust factor in students’ intentions to use cloud computing technology in their learning environment (b) Role of Security factor in student's intentions to use cloud computing technology in their learning environment. A total of 761 students from various colleges and universities took part in the study by filling online questionnaire based on the extended Technology acceptance model. Results obtained using PLS-SEM revealed that both trust and security played a significant role in the student's perceptions of using cloud computing applications in their educational settings. The study findings are useful for researchers, educators, and cloud providers in implementing the cloud environment in the educational sector.

articleTitle: Analysis and assessment of thermal performance of photovoltaic solar panels coupled with phase change material in a semi-arid climate
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: For a long time, the aim has always been to install photovoltaic modules in regions with high levels of sunlight. However, only a small portion of the incident solar irradiation is converted into electricity, while the remainder is converted into heat, leading to an increase in the temperature of the photovoltaic module (PV) cells. The operating temperature is one of the most important factors, which can be controlled using different passive and active techniques. In this work, a numerical simulation was conducted using ANSYS Fluent software to evaluate the thermal behavior of the PV module coupled to a phase-change material (PCM). The simulation was carried out for two different weather conditions during a day in summer and winter in a semi-arid area, which is the case of the city of Errachidia in south-east Morocco, by exploring climatic conditions, we were able to identify the most favorable situations for the use of PCM, to ensure efficient and precise adaptation to different environments. A parametric numerical simulation was conducted to assess the effect of two different PCMs for different thicknesses under two different weather conditions. Indeed, the results revealed that the effect of the PCM is greater in summer than in winter. In addition, the impact of PCM varies according to type, due to variations in their thermophysical properties. A maximum temperature drop of around 18°C was observed using the 4 cm thick PCM- RT44HC in summer. However, this also improves the PV module's electrical performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Organic Solar Cell Performance Using Novel Conjugated Compounds
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article deals with a series of six organic D-n-A molecules consisting of thiophene and carbazole. This series includes molecules with identical donor and acceptor groups, but different π-systems. We examined the effect of substituting thiophene (T) with phenylene (P), carbazole (C), fluorene (F) and anthracene (A) as π-systcms on the physical properties of these molecules. Using one-dimensional microelectronic and photonic structure analysis (AMPS-1D), we investigated and simulated the operational characteristics of orgnic heterojunction solar cells. These solar cells were constructed using the compound D1-B-Ed-B-D2-A as electron donor and [6], [6]-phenyl-C61-butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM) as electron acceptor. The performance of organic photovoltaic cells has shown significant improvements on various parameters, such as open-circuit voltage (Voc), short-circuit current density (Jsc), fill factor (FF), power conversion efficiency (PCE), as well as series resistance (Rs) and shunt resistance (Rsh). In addition, devices based on P3-B-Ed-B-T3-A/PCBM and P3-B-Ed-B-T3-A/PCBM show power conversion efficiencies (PCE) of 8% and 9%, respectively. The introduction of a PEDOT layer between the indium-tin oxide (ITO) and the aluminum oxide layer significantly improved the performance of devices based on P3-B-Ed-B-T3-A/PCBM and P3-B-Ed-B-P3-A/PCBM, with PCEs of 14% and 15%, respectively.

articleTitle: Characterization of Metameterial Using k-Band Rectangular Waveguide for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a method developed for extracting electromagnetic properties of meta-materials. A thin slab of fictive homogeneous meta-material the complex permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon= -1.2-0.007j$</tex> and the complex permeability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu=-3.5-0.003j$</tex> with thickness 0,79 mm loaded in a rectangular waveguide WR42, is simulated with HFSS in order to get the scattering parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{\text{ij}}$</tex> at the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{G}$</tex> band (18,00-26,50 GHz). However, To extract the electromagnetic properties of meta-material (MM) from the Sij-parameters, the derivation of refractive index <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> and impedance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> as functions of these parameters is computed using transmission line theory. To solve the branching problem that occurs to extract a unique solution, this method allows the refractive index and impedance to be determined by the requirements of a passive medium. This method has been validated by determining, in the 5G band, the electromagnetic properties of the MM mentioned above.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Vector and Hysteresis Control for an Active Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: When nonlinear loads are connected to an electrical grid, they consume distorted current, produce harmonics, and reduce the power factor (PF) which can negatively affect the quality of electrical energy in electrical grid. As a nonlinear loads and source of harmonic pollution, with a total harmonic distortion (THD) of 38%, low power factor, and weak efficiency, simple diode rectifier is now absolute. The main purpose of our work is to remedy these problems, by switching to IGBT or GTO PWM active rectifiers, we can solve these problems with better energy quality, however these rectifiers require robust control to stabilize the current waveform and generate unity power factor. In this paper we will study and compare two different control strategies: Hysteresis control and vector-oriented control (VOC).

articleTitle: Control of a Wind Turbine Emulator Based on Variable Pitch Angle with a Self-Excited Induction Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article highlights the control of an electromechanical wind emulator designed to mimic the behavior of a wind turbine. The emulator employs a self-excited induction generator, which is driven by a DC motor. A DC-DC Buck converter adjusts the rotation speed, adapting to changes in the wind profile. A PI controller is employed to oversee and fine-tune the output current from the converter, ensuring alignment with the characteristics of the wind turbine model in use. The control strategy is crafted to oversee the wind turbine power based on the wind speed. This is achieved by adjusting the pitch angle value and tip speed, aiming to prevent wind turbine from stalling. The efficacy of the implemented control strategy is demonstrated in the Matlab-Simulink environment, where the proposed system is evaluated. The results show accurate tracking and no overshoot.

articleTitle: Stability and Stabilization of Positive Interconnected Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Discrete-Time Systems Using the LP Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This document deals with the problem of stability and stabilization of large-scale systems described by Takagi-Sugeno interconnected fuzzy models in discrete-time, while imposing positivity in a closed loop. The system is controlled by state feedback control law. The suitable Lyapunov function is used to present the sufficient conditions results. Therefore, linear programming is the method employed in this new work. To demonstrate the benefits of the design process, a numerical example is examined.

articleTitle: Detecting Building Anomalies by Applying an Innovative CNN-Based Approach in the Casablanca Region Using Aerial Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Globally the growing urbanization of Morocco, particularly in Zenata City, is giving rise to environmental problems. For the development of Zenata, as a smart city, and modern urban land management, keeping an eye on the quantity and location of construction is essential. The purpose of this study was to use drone imagery and a yolov8 CNN-based object detection algorithm to detect constructions and irregular constructions. In this study, an orthophoto of Zenata city is divided into 742 georeferenced images and were separated by three distinct datasets, training (63%), testing (22%) and validation (15%). The yolov8 model was trained using the training sets that were manually labeled on construction images in the training and validation sets. The network's performance was assessed using training and validation datasets. According to the performance findings, the system trained for only three 1.600 hours, reaching its maximum accuracy at epoch 300. The model's average precision was 87-98%. Yolov8 can detect construction using images from drones with exceptional accuracy and computing performance.

articleTitle: A New Method for Identifying the Parameters of the Li-Ion Battery Thevenin Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The article addresses the modeling of the Li-ion cell and the establishment of model parameters. We adopt a Thevenin model that includes terms describing the nonlinear battery system such as state of charge (SOC), open-circuit voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ocv</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. Subsequently, appropriate battery discharge tests are conducted and processed to identify the model parameters. Initially, we began by establishing the relationship between open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ocv</inf>) and state of charge (SOC) and the relationship between R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and SOC using the least squares method. Once these relationships were determined, we applied the least squares method again to determine the value of the time constant τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> to deduce R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. Once the different parameters were identified, model verification was established through experimental tests. The obtained error indicates that the mean absolute error (MAE) for modeling is 0.0062 V, and the root mean square error (RMSE) is 0.0094 V. This modeling method demonstrates high precision.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Structure of DC Current Generator with Concentrated Winding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we present the methodology for the dimension of an innovative DC generator specifically designed for wind energy systems, featuring axial flux and permanent magnets. The evolution of the sliding contact manufacturing field and the simplicity of the generator structure and DC generator control make this structure an interesting approach to solving the problem of wind conversion energy. In this background, we develop a new dimensioning model for this generator structure. The analytical method design of electric generators is chosen to realize this model. The design methodology relies on well-founded assumptions to simplify the process of dimensioning. It's leading to reduced difficulty in sizing problems for resolution. This paper presents a global tool for modeling and determining the dimensions of this type of generator. Finally, we integrate this actuator into the control of a wind energy system to validate the global study.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in Multilabel Fruit Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Embedded systems with computer vision via a deep learning approach are becoming increasingly common in a variety of fields, including agriculture, where they can be adapted and used in supermarkets, the food industry and cold stores. By using deep learning such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in these sectors, we can improve product quality, reduce waste, ensure regulatory compliance and optimize processes, resulting in significant economic and environmental benefits. However, like any technology, they are not without their challenges. Assessing and improving performance in these systems requires an approach combining model optimization, the use of more efficient specialized hardware and intelligent management of computing resources. In this context, the final objective of our project is to develop and evaluate the performance of an embedded computer vision system via a deep learning-based approach: Application to the sorting and grading of agricultural products. To achieve the final objective, in this article we will first try to present and define the architecture of a type of CNN model, and we will build a fruit classification model based on visual appearance using the ‘Fruits-360 dataset-Kaggel ‘. The deep learning model will be based on Tensorflow and Keras sequential APIs and will aim to efficiently classify different fruit types and predict fruit type.

articleTitle: Optimal Maintenance Management In Microgrids With Digital Twin Integration: A Dynamic Scheduling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to explore the optimization of maintenance management in microgrids integrating advanced technologies such as digital twins. The study particu-larly aims to highlight the potential and opportunities of digital twinning and dynamic scheduling in optimizing maintenance activities. To achieve this purpose, a novel dynamic maintenance scheduling approach has been designed in order to enhance preventive maintenance management practices within microgrids, then the Hungarian algorithm has been used to address the formulated framework. The promising potential of the developed approach has been evaluated through a practical case study.

articleTitle: Optimization and Management of Hybrid Renewable Energy System Using PSO Algorithm: Data Center Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This electronic document presents a case study of optimal sizing applied to the energy management system using the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm (PSO), it is a management approach of a hybrid renewable energy system that consists of: battery banks, photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, fuel cell based on hydrogen storage, Data Center as load and the grid. The Particle Swarm optimization algorithm was used to find the optimal sizing of the hybrid energy system, the results show that the proposed approach is effective in finding the optimal sizing with a fast convergence, illustrating the energy uptakes over one year of data (8760 hours).

articleTitle: Event Profiling in Social Media: A Survey with an Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Social media networks are swiftly gaining traction as a platform for discussing what's going on in the real world. The amount of data generated by social media can result in a massive data stream that can be used to get insights into current events and the conversations that surround them. A group of researchers are focusing on profiling event detection algorithms, managing their evolution through time, and deploying them to work in real-time. Event profiling is one of the most important research subjects in natural language processing and understanding, with a wide applications range in various fields and decades of research. This study presents a thorough yet current survey of event extraction from textual data. However, we present a taxonomy of solution approaches as well as a summary of the key definitions for event extraction. We present the event extraction strategies over the big data era. Finally, we show up how to use NLP to outputs events from social media networks and discuss future research directions.

articleTitle: A Broadband, Highly Efficient FPA Using Bandpass Filtering Matching Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband, highly efficient filtering power amplifier (FPA) with excellent integrated filtering characteristics. The proposed technique is based on the use of an asymmetrical open-circuit coupled-lines bandpass filter (BPF), which plays the role of an input matching network and an output matching network. The proposed filter not only greatly improves the bandpass filtering response, but also improves the second harmonic rejection performance. To demonstrate this concept, a broadband PA-filter component is designed and implemented, employing the Cree 10W GaN HEMT. Operating within the frequency range of 2.0-3.0 GHz, the FPA showcases a peak drain efficiency ranging from 45.9% -73.26%, with a corresponding peak output power of 38.5-41.95 dBm achieved at saturation across the specified frequency band.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Automatic Detection and Classification of Pathogens in Olive Leaves
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop a fast and an accurate object recognition models using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). These models are used in smart agriculture applications to automatically detect and classify plant pathogens, especially in olive leaves. We start by proposing a Deep Learning (DL) model based on the CNN architecture. Optimizations for model accuracy are then presented, overcoming the problem of overfitting with four different solutions. A comparison of the impact of these different solutions is also provided. The results that were obtained are satisfying, with an accuracy rate of 94%.

articleTitle: Investigating Customer Perception, E-satisfaction, and Continuance Intention to Use of the Food Panda Delivery Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Food Delivery Applications (FDAs) grow in popularity among users by offering online food ordering and delivery services. In the Philippines, its popularity increased during the COVID-19 pandemic when the total lockdown was implemented. Nevertheless, Food Panda is among the leading global FDAs, operating in more than 40 countries, and Food Panda Philippines has over 1,000 partner restaurants. This study investigates the customer perception, e-satisfaction, and continuance intention to use the Food Panda app, thus adopting constructs and survey items from the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) and Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The study captured responses from 180 users of the Food Panda delivery application. Moreover, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed to test five hypotheses. The result shows that ease of use, expec-tation confirmation, and perceived usefulness do not significantly influence customer perception. Meanwhile, customer perception significantly influences e-satisfaction and, in turn, the continuance of the intention to use the food delivery application. The findings can help in decision-making and improving policy on the online service of the food delivery app.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Vibrations' Energy Harvesting From Cars' Suspensions and Seats Using Equivalent Electrical Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research work investigates the vibrations' energy harvesting from vehicles' suspension system and seats using piezoelectric stacks. For this purpose, a simple quarter car model is used to estimate the quantity of harvested voltage and power. The novelty of this work consists in utilizing a 5-DOF quarter car model to analyze the energy harvesting capabilities from both car's suspension system and seat. Also, based on the electromechanical analogy, the equivalent electrical circuit approach is used to implement the whole system, i.e., the suspension's system, the car's seat, the driver's body, and the associated piezoelectric harvesters in LTspice software. Moreover, different situations are studied for the harvesters' location, in order to investigate their effects on the system's dynamics and choose the optimal place ensuring both more comfort for the driver and the passengers and also to harvest a maximum of vibrations' energy. Simulations done in the frequency domain considering a sinusoidal excitation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5{{\ g}}$</tex> (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.9{{\ m}}/{{\mathrm{s}}^2}$</tex>) amplitude and a resistive load of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30{{k\Omega }}$</tex>, indicated that, connecting a piezoelectric harvester in parallel with the suspension's elements allows harvesting maximum of RMS voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$87.57{{\ V}}$</tex>) and RMS power (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$255.6{{\ mW}}$</tex>) but this connection changes the displacements of the cabin floor and the driver's body, i.e., it decreases the driver's and passengers' comfort. Also, the quantity of voltage and power harvested from the suspension's elements is more important than that collected from the seat. Finally, connecting piezoelectric harvesters simultaneously in series with the suspension's and seat's elements allows harvesting a non negligeable quantity of RMS voltage (12.29V) and RMS power (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.15{{\ mW}}$</tex>) with low effect on the driver's and passengers' comfort (small displacements' difference).

articleTitle: Intelligent Mobile Terminal Management System in African Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In Africa, the use of mobile terminals is part of the tools facilitating the exchange of data and the transportation of information in many fields. However, counterfeit terminals have adverse consequences on the health of users, the economy, and telecommunication networks. They represent approximately 20% of the global market, causing economic losses, copyright infringements, and issues for telecommunication network operators. Indeed, combating counterfeiting requires strengthening existing instruments and increased financial support. Governments must collaborate more actively in finding solutions for the proper management of illicit mobile terminals, given the consequences these devices can have on environmental and public safety aspects. The rigorous enforcement of intellectual property laws is crucial, and international collaboration is necessary for effective management of this issue. The management of mobile terminals requires not only a framework for consultation but also the establishment of a management system integrating a Smart Database (SD). This database, connected to the Central Equipment Identify Register (CEIR) of each country, forms a Smart Database Management System (SDMS) regulated by authorities. Each SDMS collects data related to International Mobile Equipment Identify (IMEI) of mobile terminals via encrypted Quick Response codes (QR). Through the analysis of these codes, the system displays information about licit or illicit terminals and compares them with the GSM Association (GSMA) database to classify them into two distinct lists. These measures will enable the authorities of each country, through their regulatory bodies, to control licit and illicit mobile terminals circulating in African countries.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Three-Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Machine for Broken Rotor Bars Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The rotor bars problem in a cage induction machine arises due to the degradation and breakage of the bars that form the motor rotor due to overheating, vibration, and mechanical constraints. When rotor bars are damaged, the electrical and mechanical performances of the motor are adversely affected, resulting in poor motor response characterized by anomalies in current consumption and oscillations in rotational speed and electromagnetic torque. This research focuses on conceptualizing and implementing a comprehensive model designed to simulate and analyze the diverse repercussions associated with rotor bars breakage of a three-phase squirrel cage induction machine. The primary objective is to develop an in-depth knowledge of such incidents' intricate dynamics and consequences. This understanding will facilitate a more nuanced approach towards predictive maintenance, fault detection, and enhancing overall system reliability.

articleTitle: Single-Input-Multiple-Output Systems Modulation Using Quadrature Media Schemes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The restriction of single-input multiple-output (SIMO) schemes is improved by media-based SIMO (MBM- SIMO), which also improves error performance by means of reducing the quantity of antennas needed to transmit a sizable quantity of data. As a way to improve the functionality of the MBM- SIMO, we use the spatial constellation's quadrature dimension in this study by decomposing the symbol of amplitude/phase modulation (APM), analogous to quadrature spatial modulation (QSM) and to accomplish a higher data rate. The Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) results are developed and used to establish the system's theoretical average error probability of the proposed scheme applying a lower bound method. The obtained MCS results show a significantly better improvement of 3dB at 10b/s/Hz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{m}_{rf}} = 2$</tex> and 6.5dB at 12b/s/Hz with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{m}_{rf}} = 4$</tex> over the standard MBM- SIMO system.

articleTitle: Reaction-Diffusion Cycles Induced by Temperature Gradient Applied to Harvesting Wasted Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The intention of this paper, is to shed light on chemical reaction-diffusion phenomenology occurred in non-equilibrium state by an imposed gradient of temperature. Further, the challenge is to investigate the effects of kinetic and thermodynamic parameters on potential differences generated. Furthermore, to realize the goals and challenges of this study, the governing problem is described by first order reaction-diffusion equations based on Arrhenius’ law—with chemical diffusion. Thereafter, an open source code under general public license (GPL) called (XMDS 2) is adopted to resolve the equations associated with the phenomenology studied in this work. Moreover, a theoretical approach is incorporated by illustrating the advantage of compartment model in describing the reaction-diffusion cycles analysis, and validating the numerical integration in the presence of Heaviside temperature gradient. Finally, the objective herein is to assess the intensity potential difference generated, and their spatial distributions versus different kinetic and thermodynamics parameters in the presence of Heaviside gradient of temperature.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Empowerment Impact of Internal Auditors on Quality of Electronic Internal Audits in Service Companies Listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In the Industry 4.0 era, there have been significant developments in electronic and digital technology that extends to all daily activities and works, including audit. It can help the audit process to collect, classify and store accounting information more efficiently and minimize risks and errors that may occur in audit operations. There is also a need for adequate quality internal auditors which can improve their performance in keeping with current developments and are able to use electronic audits to be more productive. The quality of electronic internal audits in service companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is influenced by various factors, including general qualifications, electronic qualifications, and independence. This study highlights the empowerment of internal auditors by top management in these areas. This paper uses a usable questionnaire from internal auditors in PT go public companies. The collected data will be analyzed using SPSS. The findings indicate that while general qualification and independence have no discernible impact, electronic qualification significantly affects the caliber of electronic internal audits. The study's findings are beneficial to the field of internal auditing and decision-makers who are considering introducing new legislation pertaining to internal auditing in Indonesia's service firm industry. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Selective Maintenance Optimization under Uncertainty: Stochastic Programming Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research delves into the idea of improving the likelihood of mission success in multi-component systems through selective maintenance during downtime. It considers uncertainties surrounding future mission conditions. Stochastic programming is utilized to represent these uncertainties accurately. The study presents two distinct models: one focusing on uncertainty in operational conditions, while the other expands to include uncertainties in operating time. The efficacy of the proposed model underscores the importance of integrating uncertainty considerations into the broader model, enhancing our understanding of the system's performance robustness.

articleTitle: Association rules extraction and evaluation based on information theory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Large amounts of data are invading most sectors of activity (industrial, commercial, etc.), Meanwhile, methods for extracting knowledge from data have been developed in the last few years. It is often a question of finding models based on association rules in the following form: if A then B where A is the premise and B the conclusion. We must then select relevant rules by associating to each of them a value allowing the quantification of its relevance. Most data mining algorithms use the support and confidence of the rule as a measure of its quality. We propose similar indices, based on information theory, allowing the evaluation of these rules in terms of truth and efficiency of the rule. We then highlight theorems related to a set of generated rules in order to simplify them by eliminating redundancies.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Precision Agriculture Advanced Irrigation System for Sustainable Smart Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Precision Agriculture (PA) is a farming management strategy that leverages digital technologies and techniques to monitor and optimize agricultural production processes. By utilizing data streams from satellites, mobile phones, the Internet of Things (IoT), and technologies like cloud computing and artificial intelligence, PA has the potential to improve the quantity and quality of agricultural outputs while reducing inputs and waste. This article presents a proposed irrigation system for PA in the field of smart farming. The system incorporates a diverse set of sensors, including soil moisture and temperature sensors, air humidity and temperature sensors, water level sensors, and light sensors. It also integrates weather data from a forecasting platform, encompassing variables such as wind speed, wind direction, and weather status. By collecting and analyzing field-specific data alongside weather forecasts, the system enables precise and sustainable watering practices. The data is stored, analyzed, and visualized using a ThingSpeak platform, providing farmers with valuable insights to make informed irrigation decisions.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Characterization of Tensile Properties of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP) Manufactured Using the Filament Winding with Finishing Process After Wet winding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: To achieve the highest tensile strength possible in CFRP, a perfect manufacturing process is essential. Even if the raw materials and matrix are the same, different manufacturing stages can yield specimens with varying properties. The difference in fiber volume fraction yield from the specimen can significantly impact the material characteristics in both theoretical calculations and experimental results. To confirm the numerical performance, both hand counts and structural strength simulations will be compared with ASTM 3039 test methods using Abaqus, which will then be validated with experimental test results. In addition, the finishing process and environmental conditioning, particularly air humidity, can have a significant impact on tensile strength. Without additional measures, the winding process resulted in an experimental tensile strength of 512,879 MPa, which is far below the calculation by hand and simulation with Abaqus. However, by controlling the relative humidity to no more than 50% and implementing a compression process and vacuum after the wet winding process, the optimal tensile strength can be achieved. This process produces a tensile strength of 1366 MPa, which is slightly higher than the simulation results.

articleTitle: Influence of Pad Geometry on the Mechanical Study of a Disc Brake
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The main objective of this fundamental research is to study the structural and mechanical behaviour of a disc brake with different geometrical pad configurations, keeping the contact surfaces equal and varying the values of contact angle and internal contact pad's radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r_{int}$</tex>, during the braking process under dry contact slip conditions. A predictive analysis is carried out to determine the overall deformations, the Von Mises stress on the disc and the contact pressures on the pads at different simulation times. In the mechanical modelling of the disc brake, the disc/pad wear depth distribution was determined on the basis of Archard's law, taking into account the specific wear rate, contact pressure and sliding speed.

articleTitle: TOPICScore: Evaluating Automatic Text Summarization Using Embeddings, Occurrences, and Topic Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Most of the studies published on Text Summarization are evaluated using ROUGE as a metric. Despite its popular-ity for Extractive Methods, its inability to capture semantic prop-erties makes it less suitable for Abstractive Methods. Our work presents a new method for evaluating Text Summarization by creating a trade-off between Extractiveness and Abstractiveness. This is done by using Embeddings, Word Occurrences, and Topic Detection in order to compute a global score named TOPICScore. This score is designed according to three aspects: Compression, Overlapping, and Semantic Similarity. By incorporating these three dimensions, TOPICScore is more agnostic to the used approach. We showed how our score can be computed using Arabic Headline Summary (AHS) dataset and a fine-tuned AraBART model.

articleTitle: Keeping Track of Network Infrastructure Vulnerabilities Using a Network Forensic Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Currently, new network infrastructures must support new hybrid technologies related to AI, IoT, 5G, 6G, machine learning, and deep learning, which consume large bandwidths and require the development of sophisticated recursive algorithms that allow managing large volumes of data and guarantee an optimal level of security in the face of the mass operations that companies must carry out. Given these types of scenarios, automation would be the most viable way to manage most services that result from the hybrid interaction of these technologies. All this combination of technological artifacts combined with using clients generates the proliferation of adware, browser hijackers, and potentially unwanted programs such as malware, worms, Trojans, etc., which circulate through network structures. This article aims to propose a model with a forensic network approach that allows, from a collection of data, to locate and detect the malicious code incorporated in one or several data packets, which shows the vulnerabilities that the network architecture may have. Packet capture libraries (PCAP) will be used in a wireless network architecture, which will analyze packets with packet analysis and network tracing tools such as Wireshark. Implementation of the HTTP log viewer, Sawmill, and case study tools will also be used.

articleTitle: Does IT Knowledge Translate into Security Awareness And Secure Smartphone Behavior? An Empirical View from Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study looks into the connection between IT knowledge, smartphone security awareness, and secure behavior in Bangladesh. A survey with random sampling was selected as the research approach and 678 smartphone users were surveyed. The first objective explores how formal IT knowledge influences smartphone security awareness, revealing varied impacts across different awareness aspects. The second objective investigates how awareness links to secure actions. The study finds that IT knowledge does not often translate into smartphone security awareness, however, higher awareness aligns with safer practices, like careful app installation and thoughtful use of features. Some formal IT education aspects are found to be significant, while others aren't, highlighting the need for an overhaul in IT education. These insights emphasize the importance of tailored education to bridge knowledge gaps and promote secure smartphone habits. The study contributes valuable information for guiding policies and educational initiatives in Bangladesh's evolving digital landscape.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of an NPC Rectifier for V2G and G2V Applications in DC Fast Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme for a three-phase Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) rectifier, designed for versatile applications in both vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and grid-to-vehicle (G2V) modes within DC fast charging systems. The core of this approach harnesses the converter's discrete characteristics to strategically select switching states that minimize a predefined cost function. The MPC algorithm facilitates seamless bidirectional power flow, enabling instantaneous mode transitions and ensuring rapid dynamic responses. To validate the proposed control strategy, extensive simulations under complex scenarios were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink. A comparison with a Proportional-Integral (PI) control method demonstrates the MPC's superior performance in terms of precision and dynamic response. The outcomes of these simulations corroborate the converter's ability to maintain sinusoidal grid current, achieve acceptable total harmonic distortion (THD) according to IEEE 519–2014 standard, unity power factor, high efficiency, and exhibit minimal voltage ripples on the DC side.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Level of Implementation of the Lean Six Sigma Approach in Moroccan Services
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The objective of this article is to study the level of implementation of the Lean Six Sigma approach to optimize performance at the level of Moroccan services. In order to achieve the research objective, we analyzed the previous studies from a systematic literature review, and validated them by Moroccan experts in the service sector. In addition, a questionnaire survey was conducted on 61 of the different departments of Morocco. All the answers collected were subjected to an in-depth statistical analysis, in order to provide useful information to both researchers and practitioners of the Lean Six Sigma approach, involved in performance optimization. No previous research had been carried out on the progress of the adoption of this approach within the Moroccan services. The results of this study indicate that the Lean Six Sigma approach is unfortunately not widely adopted by all Moroccan departments to optimize their performance. Indeed, 65% of respondents said they had not yet tried to apply this method in their service. These results highlight the importance of raising awareness of the potential benefits of the Lean Six Sigma approach and providing adequate support for its adoption and effective implementation within Moroccan departments. They also offer avenues of reflection for researchers and practitioners wishing to promote this approach in the specific context of Morocco.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency-Based Breast Cancer Detection System: Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Antipodal Vivaldi antennas play a crucial role in medical applications, particularly in microwave imaging, owing to their remarkable wideband characteristics and efficient radiation properties. In the context of breast cancer detection, these antennas have demonstrated substantial importance by enabling precise tumor localization and characterization. This capability enhances early diagnosis, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes. This paper introduces an innovative breast cancer detection system with a focus on a meticulously designed and tested prototype. Central to the system's efficacy are the integrated Antipodal Vivaldi antennas, renowned for their wideband characteristics. The goal is to advance breast cancer diagnostics, particularly in precise tumor localization, with the ultimate aim of improving early diagnosis and patient care outcomes.

articleTitle: Control of a Wireless Power Transfer Charger Powered by Renewable Energies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of a controller for a wireless power transfer (WPT) charger for a battery electric vehicle. The WPT charger is powered by a photovoltaic renewable energy source. Firstly, an overall view of the system studied is given. Secondly, a simplified circuit of a WPT is illustrated with the key components of the system, focusing on the phase shifter for the high-frequency voltage inverter and the compensation topologies. Thirdly, the WPT low-cost controller is designed to control the battery current in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CC} - \text{CV}$</tex> charging mode. This is achieved through wireless communication for battery current control and indirect control on the primary side by estimating the battery current. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed controller meets the study objective.

articleTitle: Takagi-Sugeno-Based Optimal Control of Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, a Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) based optimal control method is proposed for a variable speed wind turbine system. The inherent nonlinearity in wind turbine dynamics, attributed to aerodynamic torque, is addressed through the development of a T-S model. This model effectively captures and manages the nonlinearity of the system. Subsequently, an optimal controller is designed based on the derived T-S model, with the primary aim of enhancing energy capture by the wind turbine. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method, we conduct a comprehensive comparison with the standard Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) control. This comparative analysis is carried out through detailed simulations encompassing varying wind speed profiles. The results unequivocally highlight the superior performance and robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Context-Aware Home System Prototype with Sensors Management
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In our rapidly advancing world, the integration of a smart home automation system can greatly enhance our quality of life by providing increased comfort, convenience, and safety. These smart homes leverage cutting-edge communication and information technologies, employing IoT sensors and devices to continuously monitor our well-being. Our ongoing research is dedicated to developing a responsive system prototype that can promptly detect critical deviations from regular daily activities within a residence. Examples of such situations include scenarios where a refrigerator is inadvertently left open, a stove (oven or element) has been operating for an extended period, a garage entrance door is left ajar, or cooking in the kitchen is left unattended. This paper introduces the system prototype, detailing its implementation to gather and analyze data from various sensors, with on case study. Our aim is to monitor sensor data, utilizing this information in decision-making scenarios to bolster support for individuals within their residences.

articleTitle: Comparative Study Between DPC-SVM and Conventional DPC for 5 MW Wind Conversion Chain Connected to the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper introduces comparative analysis of two control strategies for a three-phase inverter integrated into a wind power conversion system connected with the grid. The two examined strategies are Classical Power Direct Control and Spatial Vector Modulation-based Power Direct Control. Both methods rely on instantaneous control of both active and reactive power, in the first strategy, power control is achieved by directly selecting the optimal inverter switching state using a switching table. However, this strategy has drawbacks such as variable switching frequency and notable power ripples stemming from the utilization of hysteresis comparators. To address this issue, these limitations and ensure sinusoidal line currents, the second strategy is proposed. This method eliminates the need for a switching table and reduces power ripples by employing standard PI controllers instead of hysteresis comparators. Theoretical analyses with numerical simulations using Matlab/Simulink are conducted to shed light on the most relevant strategy.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Animal Behavior Classification using Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The behavior of cattle holds valuable insights into their health, well-being, and productivity. Accurately classifying their diverse actions has become increasingly important in modern precision livestock farming. This study explores the efficiency of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) in classifying cow behavior using time series data from tri-axial accelerometer sensors. The goal is to detect the complex patterns embedded in the cattle motion data, providing an accurate understanding of their behavior. The proposed methodology uses the inherent sequential nature of time series data to distinguish and categorize diverse behaviors of cows. The performance of the proposed model is evaluated on a comprehensive dataset capturing various behaviors, including feeding, resting, ruminating, moving, salting, and other behaviors. The results demonstrate the model's ability to accurately classify cow behavior with high precision and recall, highlighting the potential of RNNs for automated behavior monitoring in cattle farms. This opens doors for improved animal welfare, better productivity, optimized management practices, and enhanced decision-making in the livestock industry.

articleTitle: Advanced Simulation and Design Methodology of Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers (JTWPA) for Quantum Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper examines the use of a quantum electronics Josephson Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier (JTWPA). The JTWPA presents distinctive features for amplifying quantum signals through the nonlinear Josephson junction, influenced by quantum effects at microwave energy scales. The study focuses on characterizing this quantum effects-based parametric amplification, offering perspectives in communication and information processing technologies. The results, obtained with the Advanced Design System (ADS) pathWave tool suggest promising applications of JTWPA, paving the way for significant advances in quantum electronics. Notably, the findings indicate that at a fixed frequency of 4 GHz and a constant pump current of 1.85 µA, the transmission efficiency of JTWPA decreases by 32% when exporting the design as layouts using the High-Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS). Consequently, optimization with ADS emerges as a crucial step to assess transmission and information processing before the physical implementation of the JTWPA design.

articleTitle: Hardwarely Handling Transmission Data Loss in a Low-Cost WiFi IoT Architecture for Energy and Environment Monitoring in a University Campus
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article describes improvements to a previously developed WiFi measurement platform for real-time monitoring of electrical and environmental parameters in a University Campus. The platform is based on data collected by low-cost IoT sensors able to communicate with the main server through MQTT protocol. This upgrade is dedicated to overcome the problem of data loss due to the occasional sensitivity of the WiFi communication network in some locations within the University Campus. As we hope in the future to use the gathered data to implement algorithms for energy prediction and profiling analysis, the more we suffer from data loss the more we can lose precision in our results, for that we did some modifications on our WiFi sensor nodes to get over any deficient connection between them and the destination server that can interrupt packages of the measured data to be transmitted so they get lost. In our case transmission errors leading to data loss is a major problem cause or main objective is not only to monitor the measured data in real-time but also the collection of it to analyze it in the future, leading us to figure out a solution to reduce this issue.

articleTitle: MPPT Control Approaches for Photovoltaic Systems : Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of three Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) methods: Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC), Incremental Conductance (IC), and Perturb and Observe (P&O). The aim of this study is to evaluate the performance of these three MPPT in optimizing power generation in photovoltaic systems under varying environmental conditions. A series of simulations and experiments were conducted to assess the response of each MPPT method to changes in solar irradiation and temperature. The obtained results, using Matlab Simulink, indicate that the FLC method demonstrates remarkable efficiency in swiftly responding to abrupt changes in environmental factors. It exhibits superior performance in achieving maximum power output while maintaining stable operation, particularly in scenarios with sudden variations in solar irradiance and temperature.

articleTitle: Criminality Mapping in Java Island Using Clustering Large Applications Based on Randomized Search (CLARANS)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Crime is one of the social problems of concern in Indonesia. One of the factors that affect the crime rate in Indonesia is population density, where Java Island has the highest population density among the islands in Indonesia. Cluster analysis was conducted twice using indicators from the results of the principal component analysis to group the crime rate of the regencies and cities on Java Island. The first analysis uses crime and other indicators (including demography, economy, and education). The second analysis uses crime indicators only. The Elbow method is used to define the optimum number of clusters and Clustering Large Applications based on the Randomized Search (CLARANS) algorithm, both analyses resulted in 4 clusters. From both analyses, the first analysis was considered better results than the second analysis with a DBI score equal to 0.95403.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurability in a Multi-Band Antenna Using Varactor Diode Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative method for achieving frequency reconfigurability in reference antennas by employing a specially designed antenna structure and optimizing it with HFSS Software. The proposed approach reduces the need for incorporating numerous switched elements into the reference structure while simultaneously enhancing the antenna performance in terms of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> values and bandwidth across various operating frequency bands. The proposed antenna has a small size with dimensions of 20 × 20 × 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Simulated results of the frequency-reconfigurable antenna are presented and discussed, demonstrating that integrating a single varactor diode on the ground plan of the antenna structure allows for bi-band operating behaviour with resonant frequencies of f1= 4.52 GHz and f2=5.35 GHz. Furthermore, by controlling the capacitance of the varactor diode electronically, the antenna demonstrates the capability of frequency shifting, resulting in a versatile multi-band performance with improved bandwidth and reflection coefficient characteristics centred around each operating frequency.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Control for Wheeled Mobile Robot via Finite-Time Adaptive Sliding Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this study, a fault-tolerant control (FTC) based on finite-time adaptive sliding mode (FTASMC) is developed to address potential faults in the wheeled mobile robot (WMR) system. This technique tries, on the one hand, to ensure that the system states converge in a finite amount of time throughout the reaching and sliding phases. Due to the design of the reaching law, the states of the system might reach the sliding surface. The states then slide over the surface until they reach a narrow domain around zero in a finite amount of time. On the other side, it seeks to guarantee fault tolerance in the control system while avoiding the chattering issue. This goal is realized by the proper design of an adaptive strategy. This controller is then embedded in a trajectory-tracking closed-loop system for a WMR. Finally, the stability is demonstrated using the Lyapunov approach. The effectiveness of the developed method is verified via simulations.

articleTitle: Impact of Motorcycle Placement on Travel Time and Traffic Dynamics at Urban Intersections
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper delves into a comprehensive exploration of the impact of motorcycle positioning on travel times at signalized intersections in urban settings. Leveraging a synergistic approach that integrates data analysis and VISSIM simulation, the study focuses on three key intersections in Marrakech, dissecting traffic dynamics during distinct time intervals. The analysis reveals consistent trends, showcasing that Scenario 2, where motorcycles are separated to the right of cars, consistently yields lower travel times compared to Scenario 1, where motorcycles navigate in front of cars. VISSIM simulations visually underscore these findings, emphasizing the efficiency gains achieved through the introduction of dedicated motorcycle lanes. The discussion articulates the significance of these results, offering insights into the potential benefits of segregated motorcycle traffic for urban traffic planning. This research contributes valuable perspectives and actionable considerations for optimizing intersection efficiency and reducing travel times in the context of urban mobility.

articleTitle: Application of Manufacturing Cycle Efficiency to Increase Production Efficiency: Application in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The use of manufacturing cycle efficiency (MCE), which has appeared as a key strategy to dramatically boost the efficiency of production, is examined in this research. MCE gives production the tools it needs to handle waste, bottlenecks, and interruptions efficiently, which boosts output, profitability, and competitiveness. This research finds No-Value-Added (NVA) processes and calculates MCE using a thorough methodology that combines qualitative and quantitative methodologies, through deep discussions and field investigations in the automotive industry. The results presented in this paper highlight the substantial waste that is created during the manufacturing process, underscoring the pressing need for change. This paper offers practical suggestions together with fresh viewpoints on how to maximize the automotive industry's production cycle efficiency. In summary, industry stakeholders may improve their competitiveness and efficiently adjust to a changing business climate by using this study as a beneficial reference.

articleTitle: Three Channels Splitter Acoustic Waves Based on Ramified System Made of Waveguides and a Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The focus of this research is to investigate how sound waves propagate in acoustical splitter waves using a ramified (branching) system. Three output lines (three channels) and an input waveguide form the components of the proposed structure. Each output line (i =1,2,3) has an acoustic waveguide of length d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i1</inf> and one grafted resonator of length d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i2</inf>. Three transmission and reflection rates may be computed using the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM), which is the basis of the theoretical analysis. By splitting an incident acoustic wave into three output channels, we show how the suggested configuration may be utilized to create a multipurpose device that serves as an amplitude splitter. The waveguide and resonator's dimensions have an influence on the signal's output frequency. With perfect channel transmissions, this system is able to generate a variety of waveguiding properties.

articleTitle: Integral Sliding Mode Control of the VSC-HVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article addresses the problem of controlling a Voltage Source Converter based High Voltage Direct Current (VSC-HVDC) transmission systems. An integral nonlinear control based on sliding mode control is proposed to control our system to achieve two controller objectives: regulation of dc voltage and active power and ensuring good performance and system stability in the presence of disturbances. The proposed controller performance is evaluated via the MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller effectively achieves its objectives and showcase the efficiency and robustness of the proposed control technique.

articleTitle: Performance Comparaison Of Lithium-Ion Battery Model Parameters Estimation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study focused on accurately modeling lithium-ion batteries to ensure safety and efficiency. The process involved selecting the Thevenin model for battery characterization and employing three parameter estimation methods: Simulink design optimization, curve fitting, and extraction from experimental data.
