abstract: The global industry is constantly changing and evolving technology that aims for reliability and efficiency. Modern maintenance also follows this change and can no longer be limited to being corrective or preventive but must be proactive involving the monitoring and continuous verification of the root causes of failure and predictive which aims to anticipate failures and maximize the time of repair. Use of parts based on the concept of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), which mainly transforms raw data into indicators. Our paper consists of the exploitation of the PHM concept and architecture for the implementation of predictive maintenance of bearings and gears. The prognosis process will allow us to learn about the state of health of bearings in the air screw compressor context and estimate the Residual Useful Life (RUL) of those elements. We deal with the case of air screw compressor to show the feasibility of implementing predictive maintenance based on vibration analysis.

articleTitle: Defending Against App-Layer DDoS: Advanced Machine Learning Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Distributed denial-of-service attacks in the application layer (DDoS) pose a significant threat to online services, leading to significant financial losses and reputational damage. This intriguing research paper presents a novel automated detection approach to identify dangerous application layer DDoS attacks. Four machine learning algorithms, including random forest, decision tree, K-nearest neighbor and naive Bayes, were tested on three attack scenarios: benign (legitimate), DoS Slowloris and DoS Hulk using network traffic data feature extraction from deep packet inspection. The results showed that the Random Forest classifier excelled in all cases with incredible accuracy, precision recall, and F1 scores. The proposed approach provides a robust and efficient solution for mitigating application layer DDoS attacks, enhancing the security of online services, and reducing the impact of DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Robust $H_{\infty}$ Control of Markov Jump Systems with Time-Delay and Actuator Saturation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: To address the issue of conserving network resources, our study focuses on the challenge of implementing optimal state feedback control for Markov Jump systems. These systems present complexities associated with input saturation and time delays. Unlike the traditional static approach, we introduce a dynamic event-triggered mechanism that extends the interval between two consecutive occurrences beyond conventional methods. Firstly, we establish sufficient conditions for the stochastic stability of controlled Markov Jump systems (MJS) by utilizing the proposed dynamic event-triggered mechanism and Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). Then, based on the obtained results, controllers are designed to ensure the asymptotic stability of the considered closed-loop system. Furthermore, in order to determine the maximum estimate of the domain of attraction (DOA), an optimization approach has been employed. Our approach is exemplified through notable instances, demonstrating how the suggested dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) performs comparably while achieving better resource conservation compared to the static event-triggered mechanism (ETM).

articleTitle: Survey of Gradient Descent Variants and Evaluation Criteria
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Gradient descent is a fundamental optimization algorithm widely used in artificial intelligence to minimize the loss function and find the optimal parameters of a model, so optimize the learning process. It is one of the most important algorithms for training various types of models, such as neural networks, support vector machines, linear regression, and so on. It arouses the keen interest and enthusiasm of a very large group of researchers. Indeed, there has been a surge in research on gradient descent variants and their applications in various fields to enhance the efficiency, convergence speed and rate, accuracy of the optimization process, and generalization performance of the algorithm over the years. The large number of gradient descent variants, their variety and diversity lead to confusion and ambiguity. In addition, these variants are scattered and dispersed in the mass of scientific research, which is a source of undecidability in choosing an appropriate variant. In order to overcome this issue and address this challenge, we provide a comprehensive survey of gradient descent variants and evaluation criteria to support researchers, practitioners, readers, and others to make informed decisions when choosing an optimization algorithm for their artificial intelligence project, leading to more efficient and effective optimization processes.

articleTitle: Acoustically Induced Transparency Resonance and Flat Band in 1D Quasi-Periodic Structure According to an Arithmetic Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we study a perfect quasi-periodic system, consisting of a periodicity of segments of length d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and N' closed resonators of lengths d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2j</inf>, in which the resonators lengths depend on each other according to an arithmetic sequence. Firstly, we take a single resonator between two semi-infinite guides and we indicate the existence of the AIT resonance and the resonant modes move towards the lower frequencies with the variation of a resonator length d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>. Secondly, we show the appearance of new discrete modes located between two transmission zeros. These discrete modes are located around specific frequencies with higher transmission rates and quality factors. If we start increasing the number of resonators, we get more AIT resonances, and their resonance frequencies depend on the interaction between the modes of each resonator. The creation of resonators of different lengths in a perfect comb-like quasi-periodic system gives rise to very thin flat bands located inside the band gaps. If we consider that we have (j) resonators of different lengths, in this case there will be (j-1) flat bands, which gives a general rule of an arithmetic sequence such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathrm{d}}_{2\mathrm{j}}} = {{\mathrm{d}}_{21}} + ({\mathrm{j} - 1}) \times \text{step}$</tex>. On the other hand, we study the effect of introducing five defects at the resonators located in the middle of the quasi-periodic structure, these defects have different lengths <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathrm{d}}_{02\mathrm{j}}}[{\mathrm{j} = 1 - 5}]$</tex>, the creation of geometrical defects give rise to defect modes in the band gaps. These results are suitable for the application of multichannel filters.

articleTitle: Optimizing Smart Home Energy Forecasting: Unveiling Superiority among RBFNN, ESN, and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In response to the accelerating integration of IoT devices for monitoring residential energy consumption, this study focuses on identifying robust predictive models aligned with global sustainability goals. Investigating three advanced models-Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (RBFNN), Echo State Networks (ESN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-reveals distinct performance metrics. RBFNN demonstrates solid performance, while after meticulous tuning, ESN exhibits superior predictive capabilities, outperforming traditional techniques and even LSTM. Employing Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) identifies key predictors, emphasizing ESN's heightened predictive accuracy. This research provides empirical insights, highlighting ESN's potential in enabling sustainable energy management within smart homes.

articleTitle: Determination of Polycrystalline Photovoltaic Module Degradation Rate Based on Electrical Parameters Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to determine the degradation rate of electrical parameters of a PHOTOWATT BPX 47500 polycrystalline photovoltaic module that was exposed to outdoor conditions in a temperate climate in Morocco for about 30 years. The degradation rate is determined using the estimated parameters of the single diode model, based on I-V characteristic measurements. The Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithms based optimization fitting methods were investigated to estimate three main parameters: series resistance, shunt resistance, and ideality factor. Furthermore, a step to correct electrical parameters to standard test condition is performed. From the results, we noticed a correlation between the value of series resistance and the degradation in the open circuit voltage and maximum output power parameters, which are reduced annually by 0.33% and 1.16%, respectively. In addition, the algorithms are coded using Python environment.

articleTitle: Flat and Nested Named Entity Recognition in Arabic Language
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Arabic Named Entity Recognition (NER) is re-garded as a difficult problem due to the limited resources, the rich morphology of the language, and its ambiguity. Arabic NER research is frequently limited to flat entities, ignoring the nested ones. Nested entities consist of entities that contain references to other named entities. The research reported in this paper provides an advanced Arabic Named Entity Recognition (ANER) approach for identifying and recognizing both types of entities (flat and nested). We employed a biaffine model to provide our model with a global perspective of the input by utilizing the concept of graph-based dependency parsing. We conducted ex-periments on the ANERCorp dataset, the combined ANERCorp and AQMAR datasets, and the Wojood dataset. We achieved high recognition performance on the three datasets, with an f1 score of 87.30%, 88.98%, and 89.21 % on ANERCorp, merged ANERCorp-AQMAR and Wojood, respectively. The results of this study offer significant insights for future research and further the development of Arabic NER approaches.

articleTitle: Enhancing AI-Driven Intrusion Detection in SDN: Exploring the Power of Dimensionality Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The increasing security of Software-Defined Networking (SDN) environments underlines the compelling need for more efficient and adaptive Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). In this paper, we enhance AI-driven intrusion detection in SDN by exploiting advanced dimensionality reduction methods such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP), t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). We visualized network traffic data through scatter plots and subsequently analyzed the results to identify patterns and classes. We also generated reduced datasets for training various machine learning models, after which we conducted a thorough interpretation of performance metrics to evaluate the efficiency of the models. In the final phase of our research, we employed the Random Search method to optimize the UMAP parameters, thereby improving the performance of machine learning models that initially exhibited lower performance. Our research demonstrates the ability of dimensionality reduction techniques to refine the essential characteristics of the data, facilitating the accurate identification of malicious traffic and significantly improving IDS performance. This research sheds new light on the application of dimensional data analysis to enhance the security of SDN networks.

articleTitle: Date Fruit Classification Using Transfer Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Date fruit industry is considered among the important sectors in Saudi Arabia due to what this particular fruit represents to Saudi citizens in terms of cultural heritage significance. Among the several challenges that this industry is facing is the automation of the sorting process of dates which do exists in a wide variety of types, colors, size, taste, shapes, etc. This paper proposes developing an automatic classification model capable of accurately identifying different types of date fruits and providing detailed information about each type. This initial phase of this work consists of creating a large dataset of 15 types of date fruits by taking high-quality pictures, particularly from markets in Saudi Arabia. These types include the following: Safry, Mabroom almadeena, Sokary, Ajwat almadeena, Sagie, Khlas, Mjdwal, Ratab, Lobana, Rotana, Eedyah, Safawy, Khodhry, Rshodya, and Anbar. In the second phase of this resreach, three different CNN models (AlexNet, GoogleNet, VGG16) based on Transfer Learning were considered with Non-Freeze weights. Along with these models, two levels of fine-tuning were considered: (1) freezing all feature extraction layers and unfreezing the fully connected layers, where classification choices are determined; and (2) freezing beginning feature extraction layers and unfreezing the latter feature extraction and completely linked layers. Performance results affirm the efficacy of transfer learning in fruit classification tasks. The deep-structured VGG16 model, when fine-tuned with frozen weights, demonstrates exceptional validation accuracy and excellent scores in precision, recall, and F1 measure reaching 98.19%, 97.82%, 98.03%, and 98.10%, respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multi-Robot Formation Control and Navigation Using Virtual Structures and Improved Path Planning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Formation control plays a fundamental role in many domains, such as autonomous vehicles, aerial vehicles, and robotics, by enabling coordinated movement and cooperation among multiple agents. In this paper, we examine the performance of the Virtual Structure Approach (VSA) for formation control in robotic navigation, focusing on tasks like path planning based on an improvised A* algorithm and rectangular structure determination. Experimental validation with four mobile robots demonstrates the accuracy of the VSA in coordinating collaborative robot behavior. The proposed approach improves safety and efficiency in trajectory navigation. Additionally, improvements to the A* algorithm result in improved trajectories, which produce simplified pathways that facilitate efficient movement. The paper also explores the use of Lidar sensors and the Monte Carlo Localization technique to precisely map robot surroundings, improving perception and understanding of the surrounding environment. This work provides insightful information about formation control and opens up new possibilities for improving robotic navigation in many real-world contexts.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for Diagnosing Power Transformer Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Power transformers play a vital role in ensuring the reliability of power and electricity systems, guaranteeing continuous and uninterrupted power supply. Improving the performance, longevity, and reliability of power transformers depends on diligent maintenance practices and the use of suitable methods. Maintenance should be done regularly and carefully to minimize growth and damage to internal and external surfaces. To facilitate standardized and accurate inspections, industry standard provide well-defined methods for measuring the probability of failure and calculating the remaining life of variable power This standard is standards for evaluating transformer health and performance, providing guidance on maintenance practices, and encouraging systematic improvement reliability. This review paper scrutinizes tests aimed at detecting chemical and electrical faults in electrical transformers. These tests incorporate well-established techniques such as dissolved gas analysis, frequency response analysis, and partial discharge (PD) analysis. In addition to these traditional approaches the paper dives into the artificial intelligence (AI) techniques used by researchers in transformer fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Real-time Leak Detection in Water Distribution Systems Using Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we address the critical challenge of real-time leak detection in water distribution systems using online learning algorithms. The data collected by accelerometers was exploited to identify distinctive characteristics of leaks. Our study focuses exclusively on the Online Gradient Boosting Machines (Online GBM) method following data preprocessing. The analysis reveals that the Online GBM model, optimised through random search for its hyperparameters, excels in leak detection, achieving an accuracy of 92.30%. These results, obtained on a test set, demonstrate the effectiveness of Online GBM in managing large data sets and its reliability as a rapid detection tool. The article highlights the significant potential of online learning techniques, particularly Online GBM, in enhancing water resource management and effectively reducing losses due to leaks. The results of this research offer a promising path towards improving the monitoring and maintenance of water distribution infrastructure.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Fairness in Machine Learning-Based Recidivism Predictions: the Case of Greek Female Prison System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Recidivism refers to a person's relapse into criminal behavior, often after receiving some form of punishment or undergoing intervention for a previous crime. Machine learning (ML) algorithms are commonly used for quantitatively predicting recidivism by assessing a criminal defendant's likelihood of committing a crime thus, guiding decisions and imposing choices for criminal justice officers in managing the criminal population. Beyond the prediction adequacy of these algorithms, an important issue is whether they are capable of making fair decisions. It has been stated that attributes such as gender, race, age, ethnicity, and unemployment appear to affect the fair decision-making of ML systems upon recidivism. In this paper, we study the recidivism predictions obtained by several supervised ML algorithms over a dataset that has been extracted from a Greek female prison data record. The main points addressed by the current contribution concern the study of the resulting recidivism predictions from the perspective of fairness assessment that is related to certain data attributes such as age at exiting the first imprisonment, and employment status at the moment of the first imprisonment. To accomplish that task, several criteria are applied to analyze the ML-based predictions in terms of statistical analysis.

articleTitle: AI in Preventing Dropout in Distance Higher Education: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This document provides a systematic review of methodologies offering ways to reduce dropout rates in university virtual learning environments. These environments generate significant amounts of data on courses and students, necessitating the use of computational analysis tools. The high dropout rate in university online courses is considered the main problem by most higher education institutions. Our study aims to identify solutions using machine learning (ML) techniques to reduce these high dropout rates. We conducted a systematic review to identify, filter, and categorize primary studies. The initial search in academic databases resulted in 117 articles, with 23 included in the final analysis. The review reports on the historical evolution of publications, the ML techniques used, the characteristics of the used data, and identifies the proposed solutions for reducing university dropout in distance education. Our study provides an overview of the state of the art in proposed solutions to reduce university dropout rates using ML techniques and can guide future studies and tool development.

articleTitle: Modeling CO2 Emissions in Morocco: A Support Vector Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research employs Support Vector Regression (SVR) to analyze CO2 emissions in Morocco, incorporating a dataset spanning 1965 to 2021 and featuring energy consumption, GDP, industrial production, population and urbanization—categorized as economical, demographical, and energetical factors. The SVR model, optimized via Grid Search, predicts emissions accurately, yielding an R-squared of 0.99, MSE of 0.04, and MAE of 0.19. With 80% of data allocated to training, the model aligns effectively with historical trends, demonstrating proficiency in predicting emissions beyond 2010. The study's implications for policy, industry, and sustainability underscore the importance of renewable energy and sustainable practices in Morocco's environmental goals. These findings not only highlight the critical role of ML models in CO2 prediction but also offer actionable insights for informed decision-making and environmental management.

articleTitle: An Efficient Model based on Machine Learning Algorithms for Virtual Machines Classification in Cloud Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In cloud computing, virtual machines consolidation (VMC) techniques are commonly used to improve resource utilization and reduce energy consumption. Task scheduling in cloud systems is a crucial aspect of VMC as it involves mapping clients' requirements to the appropriate computing resources such as Virtual Machines (VMs) or Physical Machines (PMs). The cloud provider must ensure that tasks are executed efficiently using the available shared computing resources while maintaining the quality of service (QoS) and minimizing the carbon footprint. Therefore, a good VM migration based on the customer's needs and IT resource capacity is required to maintain the best performance of the cloud system. In this work, we introduce an approach that leverage machine learning-based algorithms for VMs classification based on their latency sensitivity to facilitate subsequent migration into a suitable PM for better VMC. These algorithms categorize VMs into two groups: potentially inter-active machines (exhibiting periodic behavior on a daily scale) and latency-insensitive machines (for example, batch workloads, development, and test workloads). Our model demonstrated robust performance, achieving an accuracy of around 83%, thus establishing itself as the most proficient classifier in this study.

articleTitle: Extended Reality Adoption in Moroccan Sports Institutes: A Vision for FIFA World Cup 2030
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: As Morocco prepares to host the FIFA World Cup 2030, integrating cutting-edge technology becomes imperative for enhancing sports. Extended Reality (XR) technology emerges as a transformative force, promising novel learning paradigms and enhanced training methodologies in the sports domain. However, its successful adoption hinges on understanding the acceptance and usage patterns among Moroccan sports students. Therefore, this study aims to identify the determinants of XR acceptance in sports, involving a sample of 139 respondents and utilizing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) as it sheds light on the reasons behind its adoption and utilization in this domain. The findings demonstrate the positive impact of attitude (ATT) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) on behavioral intention (BI) to employ XR in sports. This study on XR acceptance in sports is crucial for Morocco's sports industry, as it can modernize training techniques, boost athlete performance, and position the country at the forefront of technological advancements in sports education.

articleTitle: A Novel Black-Box Complementary Explanation Approach for Thorax Multi-Label Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Recently, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has addressed a critical issue of applying deep learning models for clinical use by providing results that medical experts can understand in various medical contexts such as Thoracic disease classification. Most of the works that provide explainability are categorized as attribution-based approaches. These methods try to explain the output using the input features, which is insufficient for clinical use. However, the explainability based on the attribution methods is insufficient for medical experts since it does not provide how the essential features contribute to the output. This paper proposes a Discriminative Attention Guided Convolutional Neural Network framework (DAG-CNN) that relies on a case-based similarities approach for Thoracic disease diagnosis. The proposed framework for medical imaging diagnostic is based on the paradigm of the twin-system approach for finding example-based explanations. Our framework extracts global features of the whole image and local features of a lesion area corresponding to a specific disease. Then, it compares those features with the case-based diagnosis to extract the most similar cases as an explanation. Experiments performed on ChestX-ray14 yielded competitive results when compared to other state-of-the-art papers. DAG-CNN also shows the best results for pneumonia and hernia. In the explanation phase, we get a high score of 0.93 accuracy compared to similar cases. This result shows that the complementary explanation approach looks deeply into the discrepancies between outputted features and similar cases (images in the archive), which can be used for the diagnosis. The proposed framework provides an efficient similar image explanation based on important features contributing to the diagnosis.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Publications: University 4.0 and Higher Education Quality (HEQ)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a burgeoning technology that has huge potential to transform many sectors at all levels and in different fields, including higher education. University 4.0 is a concept that describes the use of artificial intelligence to modernize higher education, all with the aim of achieving quality in this sector and creating a generation of graduates capable and mastered the tools of artificial intelligence. This study presents the results of a bibliometric analysis of 78 research articles on University 4.0 and the quality of higher education, from the Scopus database. The analysis was conducted to identify current research trends in this field, the most studied topics, the most productive authors, and the most active countries. VOSviewer is used to analyze publications on the use of artificial intelligence in university and its impact on the quality of higher education. Bibliometric analysis makes it possible to visualize the links between publications, keywords, authors and countries. This analysis helps to identify the most important research topics, authors, and sources in this field.

articleTitle: Microgrid short-term electrical load forecasting using machine learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Predicting electrical load is crucial for microgrid energy management. Short-term load forecasting (STLF) helps in optimizing energy management and load balancing within microgrids. It enables microgrid operators to balance energy supply and demand, utilize renewable energy sources and energy storage systems efficiently, and reduce energy costs. In this paper, two machine learning-based models for STLF are proposed. The first is an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model with a single hidden layer and five features as inputs. The second is a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model using only load data as time series input to forecast the next 24 hours load. The dataset used for training contains real data that comes from London households that participated in the UK Power Networks Led Low Carbon London project. The models were evaluated using four metrics: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Square Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The simulation results indicated that the proposed LSTM model demonstrated better performance compared to the ANN model. It achieved a lower MAPE of 7.52% and a smaller RMSE of 0.3843 kW. In comparison, the ANN model had a higher MAPE of 8.34% and a larger RMSE of 0.4454 kW. Unlike the LSTM models in the literature that use multiple input variables, such as time and weather variables, the LSTM model presented here only uses historical consumption data to predict the next 24 hours' consumption accurately. Additionally, the results demonstrate the LSTM model's ability to accurately predict the peak load value.

articleTitle: Boosting Team Spirit: The Impact of Ambidextrous LMS Usage on Indonesian Academics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The study explores the role of Learning Management Systems (LMS) in enhancing academic teamwork and ambidextrous learning in Indonesian higher education. It examines how different uses of LMS, both explorative and exploitative, affect academics' morale and teamwork. The study employs Structural Equation Modeling to analyse questionnaire data from academics in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia. Key findings reveal significant correlations between the exploration and exploitation of LMS, ambidextrous learning, and the spirit of teamwork. The research contributes to understanding how LMS fosters collaborative learning and innovation in academic settings, highlighting its importance in modern education.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Flight Control of a Quad-Copter UAV Using Integral Terminal Super-Twisting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This work investigates the problem of robust finite-time flight control of uncertain quad-copter unmanned aerial vehicle systems. As a solution to this problem, a new integral nonsingular terminal higher-order sliding mode is proposed. The algorithm used is a super-twisting incorporating a combination of linear and nonlinear regulating terms. The proposed integral non-singular terminal super-twisting is robust against matched and mismatched uncertainties, ensures accurate trajectory tracking and finite-time convergence. Moreover, the proposed algorithm is attractive since it bypasses the singularity problem in terminal sliding mode and it reduces the chattering problem. To evaluate the efficiency of the developed approach, numerous scenarios are considered in numerical simulations using a perturbed quadcopter model. Finally, practical work is performed to control the attitude on a real quad-copter system. The results obtained in both simulation and real-time show good performances in terms of tracking and stabilization.

articleTitle: Optimal U-Net Using Grey Wolf Algorithm for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In the realm of medical imaging, retinal vessels segmentation (RVS) has a significant role for retinal diseases diagnosis, such as diabetic retinopathy, high blood pressure, arteriosclerosis, etc. In recent years, deep convolutional neural networks (DNNs) approaches have shown their effectiveness for RVS tasks, especially the u-shaped (encoder-decoder) based models. However, the manual design of these segmentation models is not trivial, and designing the optimal architecture is time-consuming, requires expert knowledge. Neural Architecture Search (NAS) is a widely used method for automatically de-signing neural network architectures within a predefined search space. In this paper, we propose the implementation strategy of three Metaheuristic optimization algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), to search for the optimal U-shaped (Encoder-Decoder) network and its hyperparameters for Retinal vessel segmentation (RVS). The proposed approach is evaluated on DRIVE dataset. The experimental results reveal that our GWO algorithm performs better than GA and PSO algorithms, which converge to more optimal solutions with fewer iterations.

articleTitle: How To Achieve Learning Outcomes and Student Satisfaction In Open Distance Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: University support for open distance learning and the role of individual factors are important elements to optimize student performance and satisfaction. However, the main problem in open distance learning is to increase students' motivation to learn and achieve optimal learning performance, despite the university's efforts to provide support for student success. Therefore, this study examines the role of university and individual factors to achieve learning outcomes and student satisfaction. In addition, it explains how the achievement of learning outcomes can improve student satisfaction in open distance learning settings. A total of 357 students from five study programs were involved in this study. The results of this study have proven that university support and individual factors have a positive and significant influence on learning outcome achievement and student satisfaction. Furthermore, learning outcome achievement was found to increase student satisfaction. Therefore, the results of this study provide insights for universities to improve their support to students and how to increase students' motivation to achieve better learning performance.

articleTitle: Integral Quasi Sliding Mode Control for MPPT of a Standalone Photovoltaic System Without Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The aim of this study is to assess the performance of Integral Quasi-Sliding Mode Control (IQ-SMC) for a photovoltaic system to ensure the tracking of the maximum power point (MPPT). The considered system contains a resistive load, a boost converter and a PV solar generator. The study begins by defining a reference voltage, where the power is maximum and then applies the IQ-SMC method based on regulating the output to this reference voltage by adjusting dynamically the duty cycle of the boost converter. Two scenarios are examined to assess the effectiveness of the IQ-SMC method: one under constant temperature and solar irradiance conditions, and another during their fluctuations. The performance assessment examines various parameters, including tracking error, transition responsiveness, and sensitivity to variations in solar irradiance and temperature. The stability of the system is assessed using Lyapunov's theorem. Ultimately, the efficiency of the developed control approach is compared to Conventional Sliding Mode Control (CSMC) and Quasi-Sliding Mode Control (Q-SMC) to demonstrate a particular interest for the photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of SMC and PI Controls in DFIG Wind Systems.
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research examines two control methods for wind turbine systems employing Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIG) in the renewable energy sector. The study compares the nonlinear Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Controller (STSMC) and linear proportional-integral (PI) controller within the paradigm of Indirect Flux-Oriented Control (IFOC) for DFIGs. The study emphasizes the efficacy of the controller in managing active and reactive power, showcasing its operational robustness, efficiency, and stability. The MATLAB/Simulink simulations exhibit the superior performance of STSMC in terms of responsiveness, stability, and accuracy, especially during fluctuations in wind speed and variations in machine parameters. The study also incorporates “Control Precision Metrics” and “Total Harmonic Distortion (THD)” to further analyze the performance of the STSMC. The findings indicate that the STSMC significantly reduces power output disparities and THD levels, revealing the limitations of linear control strategies in wind energy systems. This research advocates for the adoption of STSMC and promotes sustainable and efficient wind energy production.

articleTitle: HAR Data Analysis: Unveiling the Potential of Federated CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Internet of Things has seamlessly integrated into various facets of our daily lives, playing a pivotal role in sectors like security, transportation, smart homes, and healthcare. Across these domains, IoT employs numerous sensors that generate substantial data, traditionally stored in centralized infrastructures like Cloud Computing. However, this approach introduces challenges such as high latency, extended response times, and security concerns during data processing and analysis. In response to these challenges, federated learning, a revolutionary branch of artificial intelligence, has emerged. This paradigm shift allows machine learning techniques to benefit from both decentralized data and computing power, predominantly found in edge devices. This approach ensures a personalized user experience without compromising privacy. This paper introduces a federated Convolutional Neural Network (FedCNN) model and conducts a comparison between classical and federated learning for Human activities’ recognition. After a state of art, different aggregation approaches were evaluated including Avg-CNN, Sgd-CNN, Prox- CNN, Med-CNN, and KRUM-CNN. Avg-CNN model outperformed with an accuracy of 93.87% on the HAR dataset, while Prox- CNN Med-CNN, Sgd-CNN, and KRUM-CNN achieved respectively 93.77%, 93.38%, 93.38% and 85.40%.

articleTitle: A PRISMA Systematic Review for Intelligent IS/IT Project Portfolio Dashboard from the Value, Prioritization and Risk Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: While undertaking their digitalization roadmaps, organizations have to track down the performance of their Information System (IS) and Information Technology (IT) investments within IS/IT Project Portfolios in pursuit of strategic objectives. Therefore, the IS/IT Project Management Office (PMO) ought to be equipped with an IS/IT Portfolio Project Dashboard in order to monitor the up-to-date performance of the IS/IT Project Portfolio and consequently carry out appropriate actions. Meanwhile, uncertainty can jeopardize this performance in some IS/IT Project Portfolio key areas. The present PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) Systematic Review (SR) aims to appraise critically the current body of knowledge regarding methodologies of IS/IT Project Portfolio Dashboards under uncertainty scoping the three main areas of IS/IT Project Portfolio performance: Strategic Portfolio Value (SPV), IS/IT Project Portfolio ranking, and Overall Portfolio Risk (OPR). The present SR retrieved 145 studies fulfilling their eligibility to our research objectives. It is an important first step in understanding the current theory and available evidence in the field of IS/IT Project Portfolio performance management. In practice, our SR is a basis for devising a methodological approach for an IS/IT Project Portfolio Dashboard under uncertainty including three novel Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) with respect to the aforementioned areas.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Flood Susceptibility in Tetouan, Morocco Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Floods represent a significant natural hazard causing extensive damages. The research aims to demonstrate the robustness of employing Machine Learning (ML) models, namely Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), K-nearest neighbor (KNN), and Decision Tree (DT) to generate flood susceptibility maps for Tetouan city in Morocco. The methodology relies on a spatial dataset comprising 1000 samples, including eight conditioning factors: elevation, slope, distance to the river (DR), drainage density (DD), Land Use (LU), Stream Power Index (SPI), Topographic Witness Index (TWI), and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI). These factors were extracted using remote sensing techniques. Performance comparisons of ML algorithms reveal that RF exhibited the highest accuracy and area under the curve (AUC) values, reaching 95%, thereby outperforming other models. The key findings of this study can serve as guidelines for authorities and hydrologists to proactively predict flood-prone areas and implement necessary measures to mitigate risks.

articleTitle: Total Cost of Ownership Evaluation of Alternative Fuel Vehicles in Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study responds to the global imperative for a Net Zero Scenario by examining the prominence of alternative fuel vehicles as crucial alternatives to internal combustion engine vehicles. Emphasizing the substantial contribution of the transportation sector to worldwide CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, the research underscores the pressing requirement for environmentally friendly options in Morocco. The study fills a critical void in existing literature by conducting the first comprehensive economic comparison of hybrid-electric, battery-electric, and fuel-cell vehicles against internal combustion engine vehicles in Morocco. The total cost of ownership results reveal a key trend, emphasizing the pivotal role of the initial acquisition in shaping overall economic considerations. In Morocco, conventional gasoline and diesel internal combustion engine vehicles exhibit the lowest cost of ownership, with respective values of ∃43,188 and ∃45,449. Alternative fuel vehicles, specifically diesel and gasoline hybrid electric vehicle, have higher cost at ∃51,620 and ∃56,706. Battery electric vehicles show a cost of ∃67,005, while fuel cell vehicles have the highest cost of ownership, averaging ∃106,409, attributed to the high purchase cost. Future studies are encouraged to adopt a more comprehensive approach, analyzing vehicles over their exact lifespan and exploring the economic assessment of vehicles in Morocco on a per-kilometer-driven basis. These avenues contribute significantly to providing stakeholders, policymakers, and consumers with more comprehensive information for informed decision-making in the realm of sustainable transportation in Morocco.

articleTitle: Humidification Methods for Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cells: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Polymer Electrolyte Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) have emerged as a promising avenue for clean energy production, offering notable efficiency and environmental benefits with low emissions. However, the intricate challenge of effective water management within PEMFCs remains pivotal for their optimal functionality. This scientific review meticulously explores a spectrum of internal and external humidification methods designed to maintain crucial hydration levels within the proton-conducting membrane. The examination spans a range of physical methodologies, including innovative designs like the double-path-type flow-field, sponge wicks, and the integration of inorganic substances. Additionally, chemical approaches, such as self-humidifying Membrane Electrode Assemblies (MEAs) and specialized anode catalysts, are scrutinized. External humidification methods, exemplified by membrane humidifiers, are also comprehensively assessed. The review underscores the importance of these proposed strategies in overcoming challenges associated with low water content, representing a substantial contribution to the evolving landscape of fuel cell technology. The paper places particular emphasis on ongoing endeavors to augment performance and stability through a thorough evaluation of humidification methods tailored for PEMFCs.

articleTitle: Combination of Metaheuristic Algorithm and Artificial Neural Networks Model to Forecast Wind Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The transition to renewable energies, in particular wind power, is essential to meeting environmental challenges and ensuring a sustainable future. Precise estimation of wind energy production is essential for maximizing its incorporation into electrical systems, therefore enhancing overall dependability. In this context, this study focuses on wind power forecasting at the Scotland Penmanshiel wind farm. The wind power forecasting process with the proposed particle swarm optimization- artificial neural network (PSO-ANN) method begins with preprocessing a dataset containing wind speed, wind direction, and energy production data to handle anomalies and normalize the features. Next, an artificial neural network (ANN) model architecture is defined, and key hyperparameters are optimized using particle swarm optimization (PSO) to minimize forecasting error. The performance of the PSO-optimized ANN model is evaluated using metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R²), and weighted index (WI) to assess its predictive accuracy. By comparing forecasted wind power values with actual observations and analyzing forecast errors, insights are gained into the model's ability to capture wind patterns and variability. Evaluation metrics, including root mean square error (RMSE=94.98), coefficient of determination (R²=0.98) and weighted index (WI=0.03), demonstrate the effectiveness of the PSO-ANN model in capturing diverse wind patterns. The results highlight the significance of this hybrid approach in achieving precise short-term wind power forecasts, emphasizing the complementary strengths of PSO in optimizing the intricate architecture of ANN for improved predictive performance. As a perspective, this paper aims to be a starting point for further studies that combine several meta-heuristic algorithms in order to make accurate medium- and long-term forecasts.

articleTitle: Robust Control for Enhancing Photovoltaic System Performance Under Real Climatic Conditions: A Case Study in the Middle Atlas of Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper delves into the utilization of an optimal and robust Integral Sliding Mode Controller (ISMC) for maximizing the power output in a photovoltaic (PV) system. The research covers two distinct periods—summer and winter—encompassing diverse atmospheric conditions. The innovative ISMC controller, introduced as a unique approach, ensures system stability through the application of the Lyapunov function. Comparative simulations, utilizing real-world data from Ifrane City in the Middle Atlas of Morocco, are conducted against the conventional Sliding Mode Control (SMC), validating the robustness and efficacy of the proposed ISMC. The results demonstrate the ISMC's superior resilience to atmospheric variations, showcasing rapid transition responses and enhanced tracking performance in comparison to SMC controllers.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic based Expert System for Early Predicting of Chronic Kidney Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a dangerous illness defined as the presence of kidney damage in which the kidney cannot filter blood the way they should. the damage to the human kidneys occurs gradually over a long period. There are five stages in the development of CKD, in the late stage the patient needs a kidney transplant or dialysis treatment to remain alive. Early diagnosis of kidney disease (stages 1 to 3) can slow its progression and minimize its complications in patients. Numerous methods and models have been developed to diagnose CKD in its early stages. In this paper, we employ fuzzy logic theory to develop an expert system to diagnose and predict CKD. The most difficult task in designing a fuzzy logic-based system is to find a set of fuzzy rules and construct membership functions. Therefore, in this study we use Fuzzy C-means clustering (FCM) method to automatically cluster the training data and generate fuzzy rules along with membership functions. The system was implemented on MATLAB software. The experimental result showed that the designed system attains a higher outcome than the existing methods, achieving a remarkable accuracy of 100%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Crop Health in Smart Greenhouse Through IoT-Based Data Optimization and Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Integrating convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with the Internet of Things (IoT) is paramount in agriculture, particularly greenhouses. By leveraging IoT capabilities, operators can collect agro-environmental information inside the greenhouse based on installed sensor nodes. This data-driven approach minimizes water, fertilizer, and energy waste. Simul-taneously, CNNs enhance the monitoring systems by facilitating early detection and classification of crop diseases. Our research proposes a comprehensive solution: an online technology platform for intelligent greenhouses based on IoT and CNNs. This platform effectively collects environmental and physical variables and detects diseases in real time using image-based analysis. The results of our study demonstrate that the system architecture is a reliable IoT platform, leading to significant energy savings. Moreover, the disease identification accuracy and classification process achieved an impressive rate of over 98 %, ensuring the system's efficacy in identifying and categorizing diseases. Additionally, the system exhibits a recall rate of over 90 %, indicating its ability to identify and recall crop disease instances accurately.

articleTitle: Automatic Localization and Classification of Brain Tumors using Deep Residual Networks and MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Automatic segmentation tools can serve as valuable aids for healthcare professionals providing additional information for clinical decision–making. This can include assessing disease severity, predicting outcomes, and tailoring treatment strategy. Indeed, brain tumor segmentation poses challenges in tumor shapes, size, and locations, as well as the complex and intricate nature of brain anatomy. Traditional segmentation methods may struggle with theses complexities. Deep neural networks, particularly those employing residual blocks help mitigate the vanishing gradient issue, allowing an effective training of deep networks, by enabling the learning of complex features by aiding the network in capturing subtle details crucial for accurate segmentation. This paper proposes a reliable encoder –decoder neural network based on U-net architecture and residual blocks performing the multiclass segmentation of brain tumors. The experimental study will be carried on BRATS 2020 dataset representing different tumour shapes, locations, sizes and image intensities.

articleTitle: Continuous-Time Markov Processes for Reliability Analysis: A Comprehensive Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: As industrial computer systems become increasingly vital in various industries, ensuring their reliability and security is paramount. This paper presents an innovative technique for evaluating the reliability of such systems using Markov chain models. These models capture the dynamic interactions between different system components, enabling the generation of a state transition diagram. By deriving steady-state differential equations from this diagram, the method can determine steady-state probabilities, revealing the system's availability and performance indicators. This approach contrasts with static methods like fault tree analyses and reliability block diagrams, which focus solely on structural properties and cannot often account for dynamic system behavior. The technique has been successfully applied to diverse industrial systems, aiding in preventing reliability issues and enhancing user and environmental safety.

articleTitle: Towards a framework selection for assessing the performance of photovoltaic solar power plants: criteria determination
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Mastery of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in the realm of photovoltaic solar power plants is pivotal for evaluating their effectiveness and fine-tuning their operational efficiency. The assessment of these plants' performance has con-sistently stood as a focal point in scientific research. Nevertheless, the investigation into the process of selecting a framework for classifying KPIs, particularly through their categorization based on criteria, sub-criteria, or aspects, has been relatively limited in research. This article addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive literature review on various KPIs and, drawing upon both literature and practical experience, formulating a set of criteria to serve as the foundation for a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) method. This intricate taxonomic framework enhances the understanding of infrastructure performance for stakeholders in the solar industry. By streamlining decision-making, it simplifies the selection of KPIs tailored to specific requirements, thus mitigating the complexity arising from the abundance of KPIs in the literature. As a result, decision-makers can make well-informed choices regarding the monitoring and evaluation framework that best suits the performance goals of their solar plant.

articleTitle: Digital Forensics: Assessing Enhanced Evidence Collection and New Perspectives for Strengthening Crime-Combating Efforts in the Bangladesh Police
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study, prompted by the increasing importance of digital evidence in criminal investigations, examines how digital forensics transforms crime combat within the Bangladesh Police. Using purposive sampling and multiple linear regression, we aimed to assess the specific impacts of enhanced evidence collection and new viewpoints gained through digital forensics. With a survey of 52 participants from the Bangladesh police department, we aimed to understand how digital forensics shapes law enforcement perspectives and effectiveness. The objectives, namely (i) assessing enhanced evidence collection, (ii) investigating the influence of new viewpoints, and (iii) understanding existing challenges, guided our inquiry. The findings underline the crucial role of digital forensics in optimizing investigative capabilities and address key challenges faced by the Bangladesh Police in the digital age.

articleTitle: Infrared Spectroscopy of Quaterthiophene Confined Inside Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Combining molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT), we investigate here the Infrared (IR) spectra of the hybrids based on single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) encapsulating quaterthiophene molecule (4T). We calculate the IR spectra of SWCNTs and 4T molecule before and after encapsulation. An attentive analysis of the nanocon-finement effect on IR spectra of 4T molecule and SWCNTs with optimized diameter allows us to point out the different modifications that characterize the intermolecular interactions between 4T and SWCNTs in the hybrid systems (4T@SWCNTs). It is demonstrated that the most significant changes occur in the low-wavenumber range, and the calculated IR responses of 4T@SWCNT hybrids suggest the possibility of charge transfer from the SWCNTs to the confined 4T. These predictions are useful to interpret the experimental IR spectra of such hybrids.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Enhanced Inverter Management in Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The management of inverters in electric vehicle charger is particularly crucial in scenarios demanding high-quality output voltage. Numerous control strategies exist for regulating three-phase inverters. This study introduces an ef-ficient control approach employing model predictive control (MPC). By leveraging a discrete-time system model, the method anticipates the output voltage's behavior across all potential in-verter switching states. Subsequently, a cost function determines the most suitable switching state for the forthcoming sampling interval. Through MATLAB/Simulink simulations, conducted under BLDC motor load conditions, the viability and commend-able performance of this control approach are confirmed. The intended aim of the proposal is to enhance voltage quality by reducing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). Upon comparing the waveform and THD performance, it was observed that the proposed controller achieved a lower THD of 8.00%, whereas the traditional FCS MPC yielded a THD of 8.21%. This indicated a reduction of approximately 1.56% with the proposed approach. Additionally, real-world validation of the MPC's efficacy and robustness is provided via experimental outcomes from HIL simulations. This article revisits the requirements of a high-performance inverter through the lens of digital signal processing. We utilize one of Texas Instruments' leading digital signal proces-sors, the TMS320F28379D. Specific model predictive controllers and electronic circuits have been devised, implemented, and evaluated to demonstrate their significance in advancing a high-performance inverter board.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of an Aerogenerator Utilizing DFIG and Direct Matrix Converter Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper explores the control challenges associated with wind energy conversion systems (WECS) incorporating a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) powered by advanced converters. With the increasing prominence of power electronics, particular emphasis is placed on the utilization of a new generation of converters, specifically the AC/AC matrix converter. This converter offers direct AC/AC power conversion, bidirectional power flow, and nearly sinusoidal input and output waveforms. The study presented in this paper focuses on assessing the performance of a wind turbine equipped with a DFIG and powered by a matrix converter, which employs the maximum power point tracking technique to get the maximum power obtainable. The studied system is evaluated within the dq coordinates. The proposed control scheme is implemented, and its efficacy is assessed through simulation results using MatLab/Simulink.

articleTitle: The User Experience Analysis on Football Application at PT XYZ
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: PT XYZ has an application that provides information about the XYZ football club. This research analyzes its user experience and suggests improvements for both design and interaction. The problems are that the news tab menu displays content in non-consecutive time, there are tabs with no content, the product promotion slider banner on the main menu is irrelevant to the store article, there are icons that do not match their function, and the crash display of images or videos. The study evaluated XYZ app UX using Heart metrics and user surveys (n=400). Despite issues, results confirmed good validity and reliability (SPSS 26). Interface improvements based on findings include: sorted news display, removal of empty tabs, adjusted promotions, store menu, and unavailable content notifications. Evaluation by stakeholders and active users confirmed the improvements. The implication that occurs within this research is that happiness has a significant contribution to the level of satisfaction from the application, which is proven by the solutions provided through the redesign of the application prototype to address the problems that occur.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Lean Manufacturing Tools in Morocco: A Study on Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: As part of the continuous improvement process and to achieve better industrial performance, companies have started to implement the Lean project. Studies have shown that through the Lean project, companies have been able to identify and eliminate almost all efficiency losses that mark the value chain (from the receipt of material to the shipment of the packaged product) by relying on some lean tools and techniques. This article presents a review of previous studies on the application of Lean practices within small and medium-sized enterprises. In addition, an in-depth questionnaire survey was conducted to assess the application of lean tools and techniques in SMEs in Morocco. The results clearly showed that the implementation of lean in Moroccan SMEs is still in its infancy, and on the other hand, it has been shown that among all lean tools and practices, work organization (5S) is the most known and applied tool in Moroccan SMEs (33.01%), followed by visual management (22.30%), standardization of operations and value stream mapping.

articleTitle: Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) and Alternating Direction Implicit Method (ADI) in Solving 2-D Transient Heat Conduction Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Different numerical methods are commonly used to solve transient heat conduction problems. This investigation centers on the simultaneous utilization of the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) and the Alternating direction implicit method (ADI) for solving two-dimensional conduction heat transfer problems within a metal plate. Problems in two-dimensional rectangular geometries have been considered. In the 2D geometry, the east and west boundaries are thermally insulated, while the other boundaries have prescribed temperatures. The main objective of this study is to demonstrate that the Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) and the Alternating Direction Implicit (ADI) method are capable of solving the heat transfer equation, particularly by employing an energy equation for solid phases. Additionally, the study aims to analyze the effects of thermal boundary conditions, with a particular emphasis on their automatic impact at the interface.

articleTitle: Evaluating IT Governance in the DSS Domain (Delivery, Service, and Support) through COBIT 5 Framework at a Moroccan University
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In Moroccan higher education institutions, current progress in developing and maximizing information technology (IT) is crucial for establishing effective IT governance. Insufficient analysis of IT usage needs can hinder IT development and the achievement of high-performance results in the Moroccan educational environment. This quantitative study adopts the COBIT 5 framework, a reference model for information control and associated technologies, to evaluate and determine the maturity level of IT services in Moroccan universities and higher institutions, focusing on delivery, service, and support (DSS). Data were collected through questionnaires, observations, and documents related to the higher education sector in Morocco to achieve this. The results indicate that these institutions' average maturity level of IT services is at level 2 (established). Based on this, the study recommends improvements and upgrades in IT performance and services, focusing on compliance and optimizing IT usage as well as technical support in the Moroccan educational context.

articleTitle: Efficient Analytical Models for Accurate Peak Power Forecasting of Photovoltaic Panels under Real-World Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: A novel method has been devised to accurately predict the peak power output of photovoltaic panels under various real-world conditions, encompassing fluctuations in solar irradiation and module temperature from sunrise to sunset. This approach employs an explicit model with three pivotal parameters: the short-circuit current, the open-circuit voltage, and the shape parameter. This study introduces fresh models for the maximum power point, shape parameter, and the open-circuit voltage. Our predictive method is divided into two steps: firstly, parameter coefficients are extracted using measured data collected on a reference day, and subsequently, these parameters are forecasted under different conditions using only solar irradiance and back surface module temperature. Three distinct solar module technologies, namely monocrystalline, multi-crystalline, and amorphous silicon, are tested in Cocoa, Florida, and data are collected by the NREL laboratory. The normalized error indicator of predicted maximum output values for each of the three solar panels on June 21st, 2011, March 16th, 2011, and November 21st, 2011, remains within 2.7%, showcasing the accuracy and consistency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Enhanced Backward/Forward Sweep Load Flow Algorithm for Radial Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced approach to address the divergence issue encountered in the Newton-Raphson and Gauss-Seidel methods for radial system load flow calculations, while preserving their precision. The proposed method achieves this by enhancing the precision of the Backward/Forward Sweep (BFS) load flow algorithm tailored for radial distribution systems. The focus lies on enhancing calculation accuracy within power distribution networks in accordance with IEEE standards for the voltage calculation, while also considering various receiver types such as motor and non-motor loads. The algorithm's efficacy is validated through development and testing on the IEEE 33-bus system using the MATLAB platform. Comparative analysis with results generated by ETAP Software for the Newton-Raphson and Gauss-Seidel methods, as well as the standard BFS method, underscores the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Elastic Stress Analysis of Shrink-Fit Thick-wall FGM Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study represents analytical analysis of stress and strain within a functionally graded material (FGM) shrink-fitted assembly, considering variations in inhomogeneity parameters, interference value and geometries. The elasticity modulus is modeled to vary continuously as a power-law function along the radial coordinate of the assembly. Assumptions of plane strain and the von Mises criterion with a constant Poisson's ratio are adopted. Based on, equilibrium equation, Hooke's law, the stress-strain relationship within the assembly, and other mechanical theories, a second-order differential equation is derived. This equation accurately represents the elastic field within a Functionally Graded Material(FGM) assembly. Although similar approach have been utilized in the past to examine stress and displacement in FGM cylinders or spheres subjected to pressure, applying this approach specifically to the shrink fitting of FGM cylinders represents a novel and unexplored area of research. The analysis of results reveals the notable impact of variations in the inhomogeneity parameter n and the assembly's geometry on the stress and strain within the Functionally Graded Material (FGM) assembly. Additionally, the interference value plays a significant role in influencing the residual contact pressure, subsequently affecting the transmissible torque. The findings exhibit a commendable alignment with existing results in the literature. It is demonstrated that the elastic characteristics of the FGM can be effectively controlled by managing the values of the aforementioned parameters. Furthermore, these findings prove highly valuable across diverse engineering and scientific domains, since shrink fitting of Functionally Graded Materials (FGM) holds particular significance in numerous applications, notably in fields such as aerospace and biomedical engineering.

articleTitle: Diagnostic of Induction Motor Eccentricity Defaults in Electrical Vehicles using SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Electric motors are crucial components in electric vehicles. However, defaults in such induction machine can significantly impact the car's operation, disrupt traffic flow, and raise diagnostic costs, where many of these defaults being progressive. This paper explores default detection approaches in electric motors, focusing on employing support vector machines technique (SVMs) for identifying defaults in induction motors to mitigate potential consequences on electric vehicle operation and safety. The developed methodology is utilized to classify different types of eccentricity resulting from mechanical defaults, alongside normal operating conditions. Performance of the SVM technique is compared to other classification methods such as Naive Bayes and Dummy. It achieves an accuracy of up to 98%.

articleTitle: Predicting Adiabatic Temperature Changes in Electrocaloric Ceramics for Cooling Electronic Devices Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Materials with the Electrocaloric effect constitute a promising candidate for new solid-state refrigeration techniques. This effect refers to the adiabatic temperature change (ΔT), which can play an important role in cooling electronic devices. Typically, to estimate ΔT of new materials without characterization, Hamiltonian approaches or Landau theory can be employed. However, these methods are computationally intensive and require many parameters, prompting the use of artificial intelligence techniques as an alternative approach. In this regard, we employ a data-driven machine learning approach to predict the adiabatic temperature change (ΔT) in BaTiO3-based ceramics. The data, extracted from a survey of published electrocaloric measurements in previous studies, represents the evolution of ΔT as a function of chemical composition, temperature, applied electric field, and other features. Several models have been investigated to predict ΔT, and computational results suggest that the Decision Trees model is slightly better than the Support Vector Machines model and significantly outperforms the Ridge Regression model.

articleTitle: Improving cardiovascular disease prediction: An optimized tree-based strategy using SMOTE
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The heart is a wellspring of health and any related issues can result in serious cardiovascular conditions that lead ultimately to fatality. In this paper, we utilized three robust tree-based machine learning models, the Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Classifier, and XGBoost, to predict the presence or absence of heart disease. The dataset used is a combination of five heart datasets: Cleveland (303 instances), Hungarian (294 instances), Switzerland (123 instances), Long Beach VA (200 instances), and Stalog (Heart) Data Set (270 instances). This dataset presented a moderate imbalance in class distribution. To tackle this issue, we performed the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). The results indicate that the Gradient Boosting Classifier achieved the highest accuracy among the implemented models.

articleTitle: Identification Key Components of Knowledge Management Model for Information System Planning in e-Business: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Organizations in e-business need an information system as a tool to decision making. Information systems are a tool to achieve work efficiency. Successful implementations of information systems in e-business have a lot of benefits for the organizations. Therefore, it is better for organizations to understand the key success for enhancing the capability of information system. Knowledge management model is focused solutions to enhance competitive advantage for enhancing the capacity of information system. Component of Knowledge Management model as the key success factors for information system planning. This research aims to identify key components of knowledge management model for information planning in e- business using a systematic literature review. 30 studies have been selected from various databases to review based on inclusion criteria. This research result finds 12 key components of knowledge management model in e-business and 4 key components has been selected as the most frequently used in knowledge management model for information system planning in e-business.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Analysis of Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study conducts a bibliometric analysis of research on Recommender Systems that will be noted (RS) to reveal the most important models, topics, and publications in this field. We conducted the research from 2019 to 2023. We evaluated the data from the Scopus database by using keywords that relate to RS methodologies, applications, and fields under development. The search results yielded 87759 documents, which were subsequently loaded into the VOSviewer software. Using VOSviewer, we analyzed co-citation patterns, keyword frequency, author/institution collaboration networks, and citation analysis. High-frequency keywords indicate a growing interest in the field of RS. The study identifies He Xiangnan, Zhang Yongfeng, Yin Hongzhi, Yu Philip S., Tang Ruiming, and Jannach Dietmar as the leading researchers in this subject. In addition, citation analysis shows that computer science, medicine, engineering, social sciences, mathematics, and decision-making are at the top of the RS research fields. The results of this research can help researchers discover what is new in recommender systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of a Planar Spiral Inductor using Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper examines the application of three multi-objective metaheuristics: multi-objective artificial bee colony (MOABC), multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO), and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II), to optimize a planar spiral inductor. The optimization focuses on two conflicting performance objectives: maximizing the quality factor (Q) while minimizing the area of the inductor. The validity of the design results is confirmed through circuit simulations conducted using Keysight's ADS Momentum simulator.

articleTitle: Comparing Two Numerical Methods in the Case of Aiding and Opposing Natural Double Diffusion in a Square Enclosure
