publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Natural convection is a central topic in fluid mechanics, attracting the interest of researchers for its value in the validation of numerical methods and its multiple applications in engineering due to its significant advantages over experimental approaches. Natural double-diffusive convection is particularly intriguing because of its diverse applications in fields, where simultaneous variations in temperature and concentration generate significant buoyancy forces. In this paper, two numerical methods are used to study natural doublediffusive convection in a cavity containing a binary mixture, subjected to Neumann-type thermal and solutal gradients. The results are compared to previous studies, highlighting the impact of initial conditions and relevant parameters on the flow intensity as well as the average Nusselt and Sherwood numbers. Simulations showed that the finite difference method outperformed the finite volume method in terms of mesh independence and computational time, although not in terms of iterations. Additionally, the opposite flow case presented a multiplicity of solutions requiring careful selection of initial conditions. This work highlights the importance of understanding the nuances of numerical modeling to effectively study double-diffusive natural convection.

articleTitle: Delay-Dependent Stability Conditions for 2-D Discrete State Delayed Systems with Generalized Overflow Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper explores delay-dependent stability in 2-D discrete systems using the Roesser model, incorporating time-varying delay and generalized overflow arithmetic. The objective is to devise a less conservative stability criterion considering both delay and nonlinear function bounds. Through a novel Lyapunov functional and a derived 2D version of the reciprocally convex matrix inequality, we achieve a less conservative stability criterion within the framework of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical comparisons with prior results illustrate the effectiveness and improvement of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: 2D version of the reciprocally convex matrix inequality

articleTitle: Nonlinear Optical Rectification in Multilayered Quantum Disks: Exploring Core Radius, Barrier Width, Relaxation Time, and Aluminum Concentration Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this study, we have solved the Schrodinger equation by using the finite element method and the effective mass approximation. We have investigated the intricate interplay of parameters influencing nonlinear optical rectification in multi-layered quantum disks. By examining the effects of core radius, barrier width, relaxation time, and Aluminum concentration, this research unveils a nuanced understanding of the optical response within these structures. Our findings not only deepen the comprehension of nonlinear optical processes in quantum-confined systems but also offer valuable insights for tailored optoelectronic device design and functionality.

articleTitle: “Optimal Control for Virus Spread in Network: A Mathematical Model with Saturated Incidence Rate”
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study explores dynamic analysis and optimal control strategies for modeling the propagation of computer viruses in point-to-group information networks, addressing the significant threat they pose in the modern technological landscape. Grounded in the susceptible-exposed-infected-recovered (SEIR) framework, our mathematical model incorporates a saturated incidence rate to capture the evolving dynamics of virus spread and administrator responses. Our optimal control analysis focuses on three control laws corresponding to antivirus measures targeting susceptible, exposed, and infected populations, with an objective to minimize virus prevalence and associated control costs. Leveraging Pontryagin's Maximum Principle, we derive necessary conditions for optimal control, offering guidance on antivirus measure implementation to mitigate virus impact. Numerical simulations was carried out in other to validate our model and strategies, offering practical insights for network managers to bolster cyber security and minimize economic losses from viral outbreaks. The simulation result shows that by using the optimal control strategies in the model, the population of the infected and exposed computers will reduce to its possible minimal value at a minimum cost. This work establishes a robust framework for studying optimal control of computer virus spread in dynamic networks, merging mathematical modeling with actionable intervention strategies.

articleTitle: ECG Signal Processing for Arrhythmias Monitoring using Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Rhythmology is one of the most important and sensitive fields in the cardiovascular area, this last deals mainly with the heart rhythm troubles or arrhythmias. The most difficult challenge lies on the location of those troubles in time series, sometimes the cardiologist gives Holter ECG to the patient for 24 or 48 hours depending on each case. After the recording completion time the patient comes again to the hospital in order to get the analysis of his cardiac rhythm. When there is a lot of patients, the delay of results interpretation increases significantly. In the present study, a deep learning model was developed to classify the ECG recordings and predict the cardiovascular abnormalities with two aims. Firstly, to reduce the time of analysis and avoid more delays afterwards. Secondly, to make ECG analysis more accurate. for that purpose, Python programming language was used to develop and simulate our algorithm. The training and validation data was downloaded from physionet ATM database.

articleTitle: Internet-of-Things-Enabled Smart Agriculture: Security Enhancement Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of interconnected appliances, sensors, and databases that aim to improve human life quality in various life fields. To enhance agricultural productivity quantitively and in terms of quality, farmers have adopted the emerging IoT and communication technologies to establish automated monitoring and control systems. This adoption of novel technologies enables farmers to deal with traditional practice problems. However, the solutions provided by this new concept reveal a wide range of research issues. Since security and privacy are the top concerns in IoT environments, it's important to think about potential attacks and develop countermeasures. In this paper, we present a simple security analysis in the IoT-based smart agriculture field. Then, considering the crucial role of authentication in IoT security, we reviewed the different classes of authentication in this field.

articleTitle: ML-Based Real-Time Gesture Recognition Platform : Mouse Replacement as a Case-Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This work proposes a novel neural network-based cursor control system, using hand gestures captured from a webcam. The system will allow the user to navigate the computer cursor using their hand and cursor functions, such as right and left clicks. This will be performed using different hand gestures. The proposed system uses nothing more than a low-resolution webcam and it is able to track the user's hand in two dimensions and can recognize up to five hand gestures, which are interpreted as mouse functions. The proposed algorithm provides an accuracy of 94 % for the detection and 82% for the classification. Our work is a real-time application with 0.4ms detection time and 300ms for the classification on a low-end machine.

articleTitle: Designing a Wastewater Screening System Based on the TRIZ Theory Contradiction Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Product design is a dynamic and interdisciplinary activity that often requires the use of solution analysis tools, supported by various innovation methods and frameworks. The Theory of Inventive Problem Solving (TRIZ), recognized as a highly effective innovation approach, has demonstrated its effectiveness in fostering innovation through extensive research. Within this framework, we have investigated its integration into the product design process for engineering students. This article introduces a TRIZ-based solution developed by a team of engineering students for a wastewater filtration system.

articleTitle: Experimental Study and Optimization of Energy Consumption During end Face Turning of AISI 4140
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study focuses on energy consumption during “end face” turning operation of AISI 4140 steel under dry conditions. An experimental study was conducted to establish the energy consumption model based on the specific machine parameters, considering crucial machining parameters such as feed rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(f)$</tex>, cutting speed (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v$</tex>), and depth of cut <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(a_{p})$</tex>. This study led to a formula using multiple regression model which represents energy consumption of a machine lathe. Subsequently, the Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization technique parameters were calibrated using the Taguchi design with L16 orthogonal array table. With the goal of minimizing energy consumption, this optimization approach was performed using tournament selection. This integrated approach between experimental studies and optimization provides a reliable means to continuously improve manufacturing processes, thereby contributing to a more economy use of energy.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Mobile Application for Traffic Accident Report's Management
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Nowadays, the proportion of traffic incidents is on the increase due to the rapid growth of vehicles, making it a per-sistent problem. Consequently, the number of amicable accident reports is unmeasurable. An effective management of accident information is a crucial element, especially in the absence of an information system for amicable accident report management. However, the use of traditional centralized systems is critical, as long as they fail to present secure, transparent, reliable, and trustworthy platforms for accident's report management. This paper provides an innovative solution. It's a use case study of developing a Blockchain and interplanetary file system (IPFS) protocol-based system for traffic report management, using a mobile application. This application could be used at the time of the traffic accident. By using the application, road users can fill out the accident report at the same time as the accident while maintaining data authenticity, integrity, and reliability, and without the need for a third trusted party. Furthermore, the application reflects the safety performance of insurance companies and allows them to put an end to oversights, inaccuracies, or incorrect information when completing the amicable accident report. A better understanding and streamlining the process of handling accident reports is an essential component to enhance emergency response, promote road safety, and mitigate the economic impacts of traffic incidents, for both users and insurance companies.

articleTitle: Camera Calibration Based on Elitist Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Camera calibration presents an essential computer vision task for many applications, including augmented reality, 3D reconstruction, and object tracking. In this paper, we present an elitist genetic algorithm for camera calibration to determine the intrinsic and extrinsic camera parameters, then a comparison of the proposed algorithm and standard genetic algorithm. The primary goal is the use of fitness function minimization to identify the best solution for the camera parameters. Proposed method is robust and gives good results as demonstrated by our experiments.

articleTitle: Static Output Feedback Stabilization for 2D Markovian Jump Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The aim of this study is to address the challenge of design of static output feedback controller for 2D discrete Markovian jump Systems described by the second Fornasini-Marchesini state space model. The main objective of this paper is to develop a static output feedback (SOF) controller which guarantees the global asymptotic stabilization of the closed-loop considered system. The proposed approach will be based on the construction of a dependent candidate Lyapunov function combined with Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMI) techniques in order to establish sufficient conditions for the controller design into a convex optimization problem. Finally, an illustrative example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller design.

articleTitle: Towards a Decision Support System for Tourism Sector in Daraa-Tafilalet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Integrating intelligent data engineering and smart applications in the tourism sector offers numerous opportunities to improve the traveler experience, optimize operations, and enhance innovation. User feedback, reflecting their level of satisfaction with the services provided, is a crucial indicator of the success of a tourist destination. In this paper, we present an approach based on artificial intelligence to create a decision support system to guide the choices of tourism sector managers in Morocco. The aim is to maintain the region's competitiveness and attract a growing number of visitors. We propose using deep learning to analyze tourists' comments and evaluate the factors characterizing a tourist destination, such as facilities, value for money, cleanliness, comfort, and staff. Our method is based on two common natural language processing (NLP) tasks: text classification to extract relevant elements and sentiment analysis to assess tourist satisfaction. This approach enables tourism managers to effectively target improvement areas to meet tourists' expectations better and increase their satisfaction.

articleTitle: Random Forest and Sentinel-2 Based Approach for Evaluating Climate Change on Olive Trees
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The olive industry in Morocco's Meknes region plays a vital role in the economy, creating employment and enhancing GDP. However, climate change has led to a slight decline in olive yields. This study utilizes Sentinel-2 satellite imagery data to analyze physical changes in olive orchards from 2019 to 2023. Through the application of a random forest algorithm for classification, the study evaluates changes in land cover and performance metrics such as confusion matrix, overall accuracy, and Kappa coefficient. Findings indicate a significant decrease (29.13%) in olive-covered land area by 2023 compared to 2019, attributed to climate-related factors including rising temperatures, irregular rainfall, and water stress. To address these challenges, optimized irrigation and pest management strategies are recommended. Leveraging remote sensing and Artificial Intelligence tools is essential for analyzing the complex dynamics between plants, climate, and the environment. Hence, proactive measures for climate change mitigation and adaptation are imperative to ensure the long-term sustainability of olive cultivation in the Meknes region.

articleTitle: C Programs Formal Verification Using Maude
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we present a new approach for C programs formal verification based on the Maude formal language. The input of the proposed approach is a C ANSI standard source code. From a C source code, a pretreatment step is performed to transform the original code to a simpler one more suitable for formal verification. After that, a control/data flow graph (CDFG) is generated automatically. This intermediate representation will be used after to generate automatically a Maude system module. Using Maude tools, one can simulate, reachability analyze or verify the C code against a LTL-based specification. The specificity of our work is that we use the CDFG to generate automatically a Maude code used for both control-oriented and data-oriented properties formal verification.

articleTitle: Determination of Distilled Water Dielectric Constant by 2D-FDTD Method at X-Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a new iterative method for estimating the dielectric constant of distilled water using a WR90 shorted rectangular waveguide in the X-band with a hole that facilitates the insertion of water into the waterproof waveguide. The SII parameter at the reference plane as a function of the dielectric constant of each layer is calculated by applying the two-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (2DFDTD) method to the wave equation. The NeIder-Mead algorithm is then applied to estimate the dielectric constant. This is done by comparing the results of SII parameters. This method has been validated on two cases of monolayer and bilayer, such as air and air-plexiglass and plexiglass-distilled water.

articleTitle: Digital Image Correlation for Experimental Characterization of Mechanical Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The aim of this study is to experimentally characterize the mechanical properties needed in numerical sheet forming simulation to describe the behavior of Laminated AA1050H24 aluminum alloy sheet. For this purpose, uniaxial tensile tests in three directions relative to the rolling direction (RD) were carried out with a universal testing machine, where the 45° orientation is the diagonal direction (DD) and the 90° orientation is the transverse direction (DT). The true stress and the true strain curves of the aluminum alloy sheet obtained from the tensile test are plotted for each direction. To assess the anisotropic properties of the sheet, the digital image correlation (DIC) technique is used to calculate longitudinal and transverse plastic strains (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>) by observing digital image correlation of specimens during uniaxial tensile testing. To define the deformation in the sheet thickness direction ability against the deformation in sheet plane deformation, the r value of the Lankford coefficient was calculated for each direction. According to the values of the Lankford coefficient obtained from the DIC observation, the studied material has a significant anisotropy. As a result of these experimental tests, the parameters of Swift's hardening law and the anisotropy coefficients of Hill's plasticity criterion, which are used as input data in the numerical simulation software (ABAQUS), are determined.

articleTitle: Acoustic Wave Propagation in a Quasi-Periodic Waveguide System Based on the Symmetric Fibonacci Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this article, we have examined the propagation of acoustic waves at normal incidence in a quasi-periodic 1D Fibonacci-type structure in comparison with a periodic system. This waveguide structure is composed of two blocks arranged in various quasi-periodic Fibonacci sequences. The first block is a closed acoustic resonator and the second an open resonator. Each kind of resonator is connected to a main waveguide segment. The theoretical analysis is based essentially on the mathematical method of the transfer matrix and the Fibonacci sequence recursive relation. The propagation of acoustic waves in this quasi-periodic system results in the creation of the band gaps of null transmission, separated by the pass bands of total transmission. We have shown that the number and width of these band gaps increase as the Fibonacci sequence increases. The increase in the Fibonacci sequence also leads to the creation of several narrow transmission peaks in the acoustic band gaps. These transmission peaks appear on the forbidden bands as flat bands and sometimes as acoustic resonance modes. The precise value of the golden ratio applied to the simple Fibonacci sequence is also studied in this article. We have found that using the precise value of the gold number is an interesting candidate for creating wider band gaps and a larger number of transmission peaks than in the usual Fibonacci sequence. These results are important for acoustic wave filtering and noise attenuation, due to the creation of new acoustic band gaps.

articleTitle: Load Energy Control of Autonomous Connected Vehicles Based on ML Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Connected Automated Vehicles (CAVs) must be equipped with advanced control and precision units in order to decide automatically on the basis of any traffic condition and available energy amount. In fact, it is very essential for such vehicles to be equipped with autonomous dashboards to manage their power consumption according to various criteria related to the driving environment. Many devices on CAVs have an important energy consumption level. Certain of them are primordial for road users safety as LIDAR, the navigation sensors and the V2X communications module. Some optional features, which improve the driver comfort and luxury, such as the air-conditioning system, are managed according to the available energy and the required energy for remaining distance, as well. In this paper, we propose a strategy for automatic air conditioning system state control under some driven environment criteria based on machine learning using Support Vector Machines (SVM).

articleTitle: Experimental Comparison of Three Moroccan Biomass Combustion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This project aims to valorize and maximize the use of Moroccan solid biomass for forest and agricultural waste. To this end, three samples of cork, olive cake, and Argan nut shell are collected from Moroccan cities, pretreated, and measured. The HHV, ultimate analysis, proximate analysis, and density are determined for each biomass in order to identify its physicochemical properties. The experimental results demonstrate that cork is the best biomass for combustion because it generates high temperatures and less pollutant emissions.

articleTitle: Analysis of wrinkling in FGM membrane using the Asymptotic Numerical Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this work, we focus on the wrinkling phenomenon of Functionally Graded Material (FGM) membranes under uniaxial tensile traction using the Asymptotic Numerical Method (ANM). The objective of this study is to use a comprehensive model based on the Föppl-von Kármán theory. The obtained non-linear equations are solved using the ANM algorithm, aiming to numerically demonstrate the influence of FGM parameters, thickness, material parameter and aspect ratio on determining the critical wrinkling load and post-critical behavior. A comparison between the results obtained by ANM and those of Abaqus is presented.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of a 2nd-Order Active Low-Pass Filter Rauch Structure using Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The values of discrete components (resistors and capacitors) which are selected in industrial series according to chosen constant values contribute strongly to the performance of analog filters. A complete search of all possible combinations of value choices for an optimized design is not feasible because it requires exorbitant calculation time. The researchers used metaheuristics, which have proven their ability to effectively deal with such a problem. In this article, we present an optimization technique based on Genetic Algorithm (GA) to address the design of the 2nd-order active low-pass filter (Rauch structure). The GA algorithm is applied to the design of the filter made with components selected from different manufactured series. CADENCE VIRTUOSO simulations are used to validate the results/performances obtained.

articleTitle: Bibliometric Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Integration in Hydraulic Spillways and Weirs Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Weirs and spillways play crucial roles in hydraulic engineering, contributing significantly to sustainable water resource management. However, challenges remain in obtaining optimal design, safe management and enhanced performance of these structures. The remarkable breakthrough in artificial intelligence technology present promising options to address these challenges. This study aims to quantitively analyze the current state of the integration of artificial intelligence into the study of weirs and spillways, using a bibliometric analysis of documents available in the SCOPUS database through VOSviewer. The study unraveled interesting patterns within the research domain, emphasizing the application of artificial intelligence methods for optimizing the design of weirs and spillways. Furthermore, artificial intelligence has a role in enhancing physical and numerical hydraulic modelling. The integration of artificial intelligence in the exploration of weirs and spillways holds substantial promise for advancing the field of hydraulic structures.

articleTitle: Variable Control Gain Design for Longitudinal Control for an Autonomous Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper presents a designed variable gain control low for controlling longitudinal dynamics in the absence/presence of perturbations of an autonomous vehicle starting by modeling the system in the state space. Followed by defining the sub-set and modeling the perturbations. Then, concluded with the designed control law expression with stability analysis improvement and simulation at the end of the paper to show the strongest and the effectiveness of the controller.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Data Mining for Public Health by Using Large-Scale Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Our research focuses on analyzing large-scale health datasets from the New York State SPARCS system to understand spatio-temporal trends and patterns in healthcare. By aggregating data based on clinical classification systems, diagnostic-related groups, and spatial indicators like county and zip code, our study aims to identify significant trends that could inform healthcare resource allocation and policy decisions. Over six years, comprising 13.5 million patient records, the research identified temporal trends and spatial distributions of various health conditions. Notably, cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pneumonia, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorders were among the top conditions in terms of occurrence. In terms of costs, heart failure, schizophrenia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and nervous system disorders ranked the highest. We generated spatial prevalence maps and calculated spatial distribution statistics including Moran's Index, to pinpoint hotspots of these diseases across different counties. The findings suggest the need for improved messaging and awareness campaigns to address the steady heart failure rates and the increasing trend in recent years, indicating a necessity for preventative measures to reduce CVD incidence. Additionally, the prevalence of mental illnesses like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder underscores the importance of exploring preventative measures that could benefit both cardiovascular health and mental health, particularly through cost-effective lifestyle interventions. Overall, the research provides valuable insights into the distribution and trends of various health conditions, highlighting areas where targeted interventions could lead to improved healthcare outcomes and resource efficiencies.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of the Thermal Behaviour of Solar Cookers in the Climate of the Eastern Region of Morocco
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research, explores the thermal dynamics of two solar cookers with distinct triangular and rectangular shapes, focusing on the impact of opening the cooking systems for a specified duration. The study was carried out under meteoro-logical conditions of Oujda city, Morocco, at the University of Mohamed 1st. To assess the efficiency of the studied solar cookers, a controlled experiment was executed, placing a 1.5 L water-filled enclosure inside each cooker. While, the primary focus revolves around evaluating the impact of exposing these cooking systems for an opening predetermined duration. The pivotal parameters considered for analysis and performance assessment encompass the evolution of absorber, air, and water temperatures, Moreover, a thermal Flip camera was used in this work in order to visualize the temperature distribution inside the solar cookers.

articleTitle: Detailed Analytical Solution for Performance Prediction of Ideal Horizontal Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The actuator disk method developed by Rankin, Froude and Betz has shown good assumptions of the aerodynamic performance of wind turbines, especially if it has been combined with blade element theory. However, given the non-linearity of the resulting equation that estimates the efficiency of wind turbines, numerical integration is used as an alternative to give an approximation to such a problem. This work presents an analytical solution of the maximum attainable power coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{p}$</tex> to be extracted by an ideal horizontal axis wind rotor at a given tip speed ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> as derived from the axial momentum theory improved by Betz. This paper does not consider the Blade element theory.

articleTitle: Monitoring Megasonic Solvent Combination with Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The combination between physical forces megasonic energy and chemicals forces with solvent provides promising results. In semiconductor industry, this combination is used to make a better removal efficiency with eliminating contamination after etching. This research aims to provide the conversion from power I to pressure field P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> is liquid dependent in the cleaning process, the experimental data shows that more factors than acoustic impedance should be taken into account like the distance between piezoelectric transducer and wafer object of the cleaning process, and the increase of temperature from 20°C to 50°C affect the megasonic cleaning and improves the particle removal efficiency with temperature at fixed pressure and gasification. This study seeks to ascertain whether there is a correlation between increase or decrease transient cavitation threshold and temperature of water, with realizing some analytical and numerical simulations studies which proved a decrease in transient cavitation threshold at fixed bubble radius relates when the temperature increases from 20 °C to 80 °C. Finally, we Show experimental trend lines versus simulation.

articleTitle: Advanced intelligent fault detection for solar panels: incorporation of dust coverage ratio calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Fault detection is pivotal in ensuring optimum performance of photovoltaic systems. Faults can practically affect energy production and compromise overall system reliability. Responding to this challenge, convolution image processing automates visual inspection through digital imaging, allowing for the identification of defects from a sequence of images. This study introduces a comprehensive approach for smart detection of fault in solar panels. Therefore artificial intelligence techniques are applied, utilizing YOLO_NAS for defect identification and employing OpenCV for dust coverage rate calculation. The achieved results by using YOLO_NAS model for fault detection demonstrate significant precision and recall values, reaching 0.96 and 0.89, respectively. These findings confirm the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in smartly detecting faults, including dust, and accurately quantifying the dust coverage. This approach is promising for the management and maintenance of solar photovoltaic systems by enhancing their reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband LNA Based on Various Distributed-Element Microwave Filters With Semi-Distributed Notch Filtering for Interference Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In this paper, we have modeled a low-noise amplifier that we have adapted using a multisection filter at the input, a distributed-element bandpass coupled-resonator filter at the output, and a third notch filter for interference rejection. Results show that the amplifier is unconditionally stable over the entire [1.8-3] GHz band. In addition, the gain is satisfactory, and the reflection coefficients S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf> at the input and output are low. This modeled amplifier can be integrated into systems dedicated to Wi-Fi, while also offering possibilities for use in other applications such as wireless communications, wireless sensor technologies, telemetry systems, and remote monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Resilience: A Deep Learning Approach to Late Delivery Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach to predict late delivery risks, aiming to strengthen supply chain resilience through smart, data-driven strategies. The approach combines clustering using the Elbow method and multiclassification, incorporating advanced deep learning models like Neural Network(NN), Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). The findings highlight the effectiveness of the (CNN-LSTM) model in producing more accurate results, ultimately improving supply chain resilience, boosting customer satisfaction, and enabling proactive risk management.

articleTitle: Polynomial Metamodelling of Computer Simulation for UAV Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Statistical technics and regressions methods, has gained more attention and developments in the field of machine learning, giving rise to new approaches and tools. In the case of aeronautical engineering, and in similar industries, these innovative technics aid to efficiently analyze large amount of data and achieve feasible designs. Here a Polynomial model construction is investigated. It is shown that combining cross validation and statistical tests methods results in satisfactory model accuracy with less tremendous computations. Some post processing is then used to locate feasible design variables ranges for longitudinal static stability of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV).

articleTitle: Towards a Warehouse 4.0: Proposal of a Maturity Model for SMEs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Warehousing stands as a cornerstone of logistics infrastructure, exerting a profound influence on the competitive landscape of industries worldwide. Recognizing its pivotal role, this research endeavors to enhance warehouse performance through the strategic integration of a maturity model and cutting-edge Industry 4.0 technologies.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and Evaluation of Francis Type Turbine Alternators using the Multi-Sensor Vibration Analysis Approach: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: For industry 4.0, vibration analysis is crucial in the diagnosis of mechanical systems, thanks to its ability to identify anomalies, whether structural or operational. This article aims to explain in detail this method of analysis on a hydroelectric generator. Through the exploration of eight distinct operating modes, the collection of specific vibration data, and an in-depth understanding of the system's reactions under varied conditions. This data is then subjected to careful evaluation to determine overall speed and travel levels. This critical step provides a comprehensive assessment of overall alternator performance and behavior. This detailed analysis constitutes a solid basis for assessing the state of health of the alternator, anticipating possible failures, and recommending preventive and corrective actions. To ensure the credibility of the results obtained, validation is carried out in accordance with the rigorous standards established by ISO 10816-5 and ISO 7919-5. This approach guarantees the reliability and precision of the confidence of the system studied in order to give recommendations formulated to maintain reliability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Comprehensive Criteria Hierarchy for Data Analytics Use Cases’ Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Data-driven transformation has become a necessary step towards sustainable change and a major accelerator of companies' progress. In this journey, one of the early challenges companies are confronted to prioritizing the initiatives in an effective fashion. Many conventional techniques have been used to prioritize IT projects, and some were slightly adapted to handle data analytics use cases specifically, but decision makers mostly rely on their expertise and understanding of the company's objectives and constraints to put the use cases in order. This paper digs further in this topic by reviewing the prioritization techniques available today, discussing how these techniques and their criteria fit in the context of data analytics use cases. It then, proposes a comprehensive criteria hierarchy that can be used by a scoring model or a hierarchical multi-criteria method such as AHP to provide better guidance to decision makers for the prioritization of data analytics use cases.

articleTitle: Assessing Requirements Engineering Practices' Impact on Electronic Government Solution Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: E-Government initiatives leverage Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs) to enhance governmental efficiency and facilitate online service provision. Software Requirements Engineering (RE) plays a critical role in ensuring the success of these initiatives by identifying, analyzing, documenting, validating, and managing project requirements. Despite the potential benefits, challenges persist in implementing RE practices effectively within E-Government projects. This article explores the importance of RE in E-Government, highlighting the need for early integration of RE methods to address challenges and optimize project outcomes. Through a systematic literature review, key factors contributing to E-Government project success and failure are identified, emphasizing the role of robust RE practices in mitigating risks and maximizing success. The analysis reveals deficiencies in the current literature, including limited empirical studies, insufficient focus on stakeholder engagement, and the absence of standardized frameworks. By bridging these gaps, practitioners can enhance the development and implementation of E-Government solutions through effective RE methodologies.

articleTitle: Maintenance and Production Optimization using artificial intelligence (AI) Tools: A Bibliometric Analysis and Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The ever-present challenge of optimizing production efficiency and maintenance effectiveness lies at the heart of a company's smooth operations. These two functions are intricately linked, with efficient production relying on well-maintained equipment and effective maintenance minimizing production disruptions. In this context, it is important to analyze the methods used to optimize these two services as part of the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) tools. In this regard, based on recent literature, the main objective of this paper is to present an overview of the evolution of the use of AI tools in the optimization of maintenance and production. It also studied the AI tools most recommended by researchers. For this purpose, we will successively analyze the sorting and classification of the recent literature according to the established criteria, then, we will present and discuss the AI methods used for the optimization of maintenance and production, to conclude with a conclusion of the bibliography and the suggestions for future research.

Author Keywords: artificial intelligence, production, optimization, maintenance, bibliometric analysis

articleTitle: 3D CNN-BN: A Breakthrough in Colorectal Cancer Detection with Deep Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The Convolutional neural network (CNN) has made significant strides in the medical domain. CNN excels at the extraction of highly representative features in acute medical pathology. Amidst the network layers, CNN allows classification Through the process of filtering, selecting, and implementing these characteristics at the final layer level that is fully connected. Colon cancer rises from cells that cover the inner lining of the colon. Frequently originating from a noncancerous growth known as a polyp, it progresses gradually and eventually becomes cancerous. Our study aims to develop a computer-aided detection (CAD) system using a CT colonography dataset for colorectal cancer (CRC) prevention by classifying scans as polyp or polyp-free. After the preprocessing phase, we developed a deep-learning model with two variations: a 3D CNN-BN and a 3D CNN-BN & Dropout. 3D CT images of the abdomen classification according to the presence of polyps or its absence using CNN is primordial to enhance the chance of early detection. Thus, move toward the appropriate treatment. Our primary emphasis is on enhancing the training process of deep learning models and improving their performance during the testing phase. The findings suggest that the 3DCNN-BN demonstrated superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 92%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Photovoltaic System Efficiency Through a Kalman Filter Driven Approach for MPPT in Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: An electronic tool, referred to as an MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracker), is designed to harness the utmost power from a PV module, even amidst varying environmental conditions. However, numerous traditional MPPT techniques face challenges in accurately capturing maximum power when confronted with partial shading scenarios. Partial shading is a common challenge in PV systems, typically occurring when certain portions of interconnected series strings are shaded. This situation leads to the presence of multiple peaks in the Power-Voltage (P-V) characteristic curve of the PV system. Consequently, to pursue the maximum power under partial shading conditions, a stochastic search method called Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is utilized instead of traditional techniques. However, it's important to highlight that the PSO method has a drawback due to its relatively slow operation. Consequently, this research presents an innovative Kalman filter methodology pivotal for accelerating the Maximum Power Point (MPP) tracking by minimizing errors. The study re-evaluates the prerequisites of an elite boost converter with a focus on digital signal processing. Leveraging the prowess of Texas Instruments, we employ the renowned digital signal processor, TMS320F28379D. Tailored Kalman filter techniques, combined with PSO methods and specialized electronic circuits, have been conceptualized, executed, and assessed, underscoring their pivotal role in elevating the performance of the converter board. The proposed Kalman filter significantly enhances dynamic tracking efficiency, surpassing PSO by over 10% and PandO by 30%. Additionally, it markedly reduces tracking time, achieving up to a 99.998% decrease compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Automatic Collection System for Medical Consultation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The increasing demand for medical consultations, coupled with the growing population and the detection of new pandemics such as Covid-19, has put a strain on hospitals and physicians. New technologies, like IoT, AI etc., can help to optimize consultations and relieve physicians and nurses of some of their manual more advanced tasks. In this work we developed an IoT -Based device called, Smart Medical Gate (SMG) that uses sensors to automatically collect physiological data from patients and store them in to a dedicated database (It could be on a Health Information System (HIS) of the facility or on a cloud). In this work we store the data collected by the SMG on a cloud. The data is then made available to health professional, allowing them to quickly access it to facilitate the consultation process. The SMG can also be used for teleconsultations, which can help to reduce the need for in-person appointments to avoid contaminations in Covid-19 pandemic or other pandemic and also this is especially beneficial for patients who live in rural areas or who have difficulty traveling. By automating the collection of patient data and making it more ac-accessible to physicians, the SMG can help to improve the efficiency of medical consultations. It will allow the medical professionals to focus on patient care as well as moral and psychological support, something that no machine in the world can do until now.

articleTitle: Exploratory Literature Review of Maturity Models in Industry 4.0 and 5.0
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In the present era, the manufacturing sector is experiencing two distinct revolutions. Industry 4.0 emphasizes machine autonomy, digitization, and problem-solving without human intervention. On the other hand, industry 5.0 represents a paradigm shift that goes beyond productivity and efficiency, focusing on reintegrating humans into the production process and recognizing their value. To remain competitive, companies must keep up with these trends and advancements. Initially, they faced challenges in adapting to the automation level of industry 4.0, but now they must embrace the new era to enhance their performance. Consequently, it is crucial to assess the maturity level of the industry in order to establish a roadmap for implementing industry 5.0. This paper conducts an exploratory literature review of 106 research papers, selected from a pool of 181 publications obtained from Scopus and Web of Science databases and analyzed in NVIVO. The study occurs qualitative research by analyzing word usage through word cloud, delve into connections between those words in particular subjects and examine existing maturity models. This study guided us towards a focal point where the intersection of Industry 5.0 and manufacturing maturity models promises rich opportunities for investigation and contribution.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Integration and Green Hydrogen Prospects in Morocco: A Comprehensive Analysis of Energy Transition Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper investigates Morocco's energy transition, focusing on its commitment to renewable energy and the emerging sector of Green Hydrogen. Leveraging geographical advantages such as abundant solar and wind resources, Morocco has positioned itself as a leader in concentrated solar power (CSP) and wind energy production. The study employs a systematic methodology, including a literature review and comprehensive data collection, to analyze Morocco's oil and natural gas reserves, electricity demand trends, and electricity market dynamics. While renewable energy constitutes over 10% of electricity production, Morocco remains dependent on fossil fuels. The paper further explores the potential of Green Hydrogen, examining demand projections and Morocco's National Roadmap for Green Hydrogen (NRGH). The NRGH outlines ambitious plans for green hydrogen production, positioning Morocco as a key player in the global market. The study concludes by highlighting the implications of the findings and recommending a holistic approach for Morocco's transition to a sustainable and low-carbon energy system.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Materials Used In Marine Engineering: Advances, Challenges and Practices
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This article provides a comprehensive review of the current state of design and materials used in shipbuilding. It explores various types of vessels and innovative materials such as composites and steel employed in their construction. Additionally, the article examines different material tests discussed in the literature and their relevance in the maritime field. Ship corrosion is also addressed, with particular focus on mitigation strategies. Finally, the environmental impact of ships is discussed, highlighting implications and measures to minimize this impact.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Dose and Radiogenic Risk Reductions During Brain CT Angiography
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The objective of this investigation was to assess and quantify the dose reduction to the thyroid gland and eye lens in pediatric brain Computed tomography angiography (CTA) examinations. This evaluation was conducted before and after implementing thyroid and eye lens shielding and deactivating the tube current modulation (ATCM) techniques. Additionally, the study aimed to evaluate the radiogenic risk associated with these protocols. An experimental inquiry was carried out employing the CIRS ATOM phantom in conjunction with a multi-slice 16 CT scanner. Dosimetry was executed utilizing optically stimulated luminescence dosimeters (OSL) chips. The investigation encompassed the application of circumferential thyroid and eye lens shielding, facilitating a comparative examination against unshielded conditions and the deactivation of ATCM techniques. The introduction of protective materials yielded a substantial 77.51% reduction in lens dose, concurrently lowering the risk of radiation-induced cancer development in the lenses by 77.5%. This transitioned the rate from 3 procedures per 1000 to 6.78 procedures per 10000 Conversely, deactivating the ATCM techniques led to significant dose increases in the thyroid, eye lens, and entrance dose by 50%, 24.3%, and 50.26%, respectively. Notably, the deactivation of ATCM resulted in a 24.3% rise in radiogenic risks to the lens, shifting the rate from 3 per 1000 procedures to 3.74 per 1000 procedures. Similarly, the radiogenic risk to the thyroid gland experienced a 47% escalation, progressing from 23 to 34 procedures per 100000.

articleTitle: Application of Variable Selection Method (Stepwise Regression Analysis) to Forecast the $\mathrm{P}{{\mathrm{M}}_{10}}$ Concentrations in Agadir City (Morocco)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Many countries are preoccupied with the high concentrations of particulate matter PM10, due to the rapid industrialization which can be harmful to people's health and the environment. The capacity to predict these particulate matters in advance allows for better planning to avoid and decrease their impact. This is possible and attainable if we have a good grasp of the contaminants present in the air and the factors that determine their patterns. A great deal of research indicates that pollutant pattern is influenced by meteorological parameters such as wind speed (WS), relative humidity (H), and temperature (T). Statistically, the correlation between these parameters is significant in most cases. The present study aims to use the stepwise regression method for forecasting ambient PM10 in the city of Agadir, Morocco, based on the data collected from a fixed station placed at a school, in Agadir city center during two years (2009-2010). The goodness of fit, which implies a comparison of the observed and the predicted values, is studied through performance indicators using the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R2). In the face of the difficulty in synthesizing and interpreting certain scores due to the diversity of the parameters used in their computations, and the fact that the scores do not all point in the same direction, we were able to come up with satisfactory results in the evaluation of the used model <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\mathrm{R}2 = 0.64,\text{RMSE} = 9.224,\text{MSE} = 85.088,\text{MAE} = 6.687})$</tex>. This shows the ability of the stepwise regression model to predict the next day PM10 concentration.

articleTitle: Sustainability in the Era of Industry 4.0 and Circular Economy: Thoretical Background and Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The emergence of the sustainable development has encouraged manufacturers and scientific researchers to adopt new economic models such as the “circular economy”. This new strategy targets the efficient and sustainable management of resources as well as the reduction and elimination of waste. Researches on circularity in business models has recently increased but few researchers have studied the link between sustainability and circular economy in the context of Industry 4.0. To fill this gap, this paper conducts a bibliometric analysis to identify and discuss the existing literature. This review, based on the Scopus database, identified a literature survey of 77 documents published from 2017 to 2023. The paper begins by defining the different concepts related to our studies. Thereafter, it highlights our research methodology steps, followed by descriptive analysis. The findings indicate that there is a clear orientation of sustainability to improve manufacturing system and supply chain management throughout the product life cycle. Also, the industry 4.0 technologies are necessary to implement the circular economy strategies. Thus, organizations will be able to build a cleaner-intelligent processes.

articleTitle: Exploring Machine Learning Approaches for Breast Cancer Prediction: A Comparative Analysis with ANOVA-Based Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: A widespread issue across the globe, breast cancer impacts women across diverse regions and populations. Early detection remains crucial for improving treatment outcomes and reducing mortality rates associated with the disease. Advancements in technology, especially in Machine Learning (ML), present promising opportunities to enhance the accuracy and effectiveness of breast cancer detection methods. The research carried out in this investigation involves a comparative analysis of three ML models (DT, ANN, SVM), utilizing the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset incorporating ANOVA for feature selection. The primary objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of these models in achieving precise and timely breast cancer detection. Through a comprehensive assessment, which includes common metrics, our findings underscore the superior performance of the SVM model, achieving a precision, recall, and F1-score of 98.59%. These results underscore the SVM's potential for accurate and early prediction of breast cancer using this dataset. This research contributes to advancing our understanding of machine learning methodologies in breast cancer diagnosis, emphasizing the significant role of technology and ML in facilitating early detection and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Revisiting the Effect of the Interatomic Potentials in the Simulated Calcium Silicate Glasses
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Calcium silicate glasses (CaO)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>-(SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>, are of particular interest as they form the backbone of a variety of multi-components industrial and natural glasses. Their study bridges the gap in the more explored field of calcium-alumino silicate glasses. Here, we have assessed the effect of interatomic potential on the structural, transport and mechanical properties of calcium silicate glasses using molecular dynamics simulations. By using three different potentials (two-, and three- body interactions) and comparing the simulated properties with experimental data we show that the structure of the simulated glasses does not strongly depend on the type and calibration of the potential set. However, the mechanical and transport properties are sensitive to the interatomic potential. The potential sets can reproduce the compositional dependence of the elastics constants (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</inf>) but with a large relative error values. Similarly, for the transport properties, the three-body potential fails to reproduce the dynamics of the atoms, whereas, the two body potential fairly predicts the atomic displacement of the atoms. Thus, the potential calibrated with dynamics and thermodynamics properties can successfully produce the shape of experimental data.

articleTitle: Teaching Cybersecurity to Engineering Students: A New Perspective Through Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: In today's fast-changing world of cybersecurity threats, and specifically the dynamic domain of cybersecurity education which is characterized by constant flux in the digital landscape, understanding and effectively responding to emerging challenges are critical imperatives. With a specific focus on data-driven methodologies, this literature review aims to unravel patterns and insights without delving into the analysis of human responses. The objective is to synthesize current knowledge and identify gaps for potential future research. This paper undertakes a rigorous systematic literature review, analyzing 220 publications with 73 specifically addressing cybersecurity education retrieved from esteemed databases such as Scopus. For a thorough examination, the study employs quantitative and qualitative research methods. Notably, it delves into a focused exploration of word usage through the creation of word clouds, probes the interconnections among these words within specific subjects, and scrutinizes established maturity models.

articleTitle: High Resolution Panoramic Video Synthesis and Objects Detection on Panoramic Video
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: We propose an approach to the creation of a panorama viewport and objects detection within it in real-time on the base of the set of videos from the assembly of cameras. The task of the panorama viewport generation is significantly different from the panoramic image generation. We perform image stitching only with a part of cameras views (region of interest - ROI) and display the resulting images flow on the user's screen. The complexity of this problem is in processing the images from the set of cameras at the moment, since it is impossible to stitch, process and save the whole panorama in the user device memory. The main practical application of the proposed technology is video surveillance for transportation, industry and public objects (airports, railway stations, sea and river ports, plants, stadiums, etc.). Nowadays, there are many scientific articles exploring panorama stitching methods. However, not many existing algorithms can be used for the panorama stitching in real-time as is. Real-time panorama stitching is the value of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Radiation Safety in Moroccan Healthcare: A Comprehensive Study on X-Ray Dose Monitoring, Control, and Dosimeter Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Ensuring the strict oversight and surveillance of X-ray doses emerges not merely as a regulatory necessity but as an urgent concern for both Moroccan healthcare institutions and regulatory authorities. This paper introduces an empirical investigation that delves deep into the rigorous control and monitoring of X-ray dosimetry within the context of Moroccan healthcare establishments. The study's findings underscore a notable observation: a substantial 62% of healthcare professionals across various organizations are exposed to ionizing radiation, lacking fundamental knowledge of radiation protection measures. This alarming revelation emphasizes an immediate need for heightened awareness and continuous training initiatives for healthcare professionals in the domain of radiation protection. Simultaneously, it calls for the urgent implementation of essential protective measures. Then, employing a comprehensive approach involving case studies, data analysis, and comparative assessments, this paper evaluates the efficacy of diverse control and monitoring strategies. The study offers practical insights and recommendations tailored for healthcare practitioners and administrators, aiming to elevate radiation safety protocols within Moroccan hospitals. Ultimately, this research aspires to contribute to the evolution of optimal practices in X-ray dose management, fostering a culture of safety and ensuring the delivery of high-quality healthcare services in the Moroccan medical field.

articleTitle: Enhancing Reusability in Microservice Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This research delves into the domain of microservices, with a primary focus on elevating reusability within microservice architectures. Microservices have emerged as a promising solution to address the limitations of monolithic legacy systems, offering heightened agility, improved maintainability, and a means to overcome complexities in software development. However, reusability in microservices remains a critical concern due to several challenges, including Code Duplication, Technology Heterogeneity, Service Boundaries, Contextual Dependencies, Interface Design, and Versioning. To mitigate these challenges, we introduce the Reusable Microservices Framework, a systematic software development process based on principles distinct from Domain-Driven Decomposition. The validation of the RMF comprises a two-phase approach. In the first phase, we substantiated its effectiveness through a mathematical proof, highlighting a notable reduction in development time. In the second phase, we implemented the RMF in a real-world software company, demonstrating its practical adoption and impact on enhancing reusability and agility in the ever-evolving digital landscape.

articleTitle: Green Energy and Blockchain: Sustainable Technology Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Today, the concept of green energy has a critical role in achieving sustainability goals. The effective utilization of green energy resources and the management of energy from generation to distribution has become a key priority of sustainable energy transformation today. In this context, the use of blockchain technology provides an important infrastructure for transparent and secure management of energy processes. Blockchain is known as distributed ledger technology and represents a database that is updated simultaneously between many computers on a network. This technology is used in many application areas, ensuring data integrity and security. In the green energy sector, the use of blockchain technology is possible in various scenarios. Issues such as more effective use of green energy resources, monitoring and verifying energy consumption, and reducing carbon emissions include potential applications of blockchain in this field. The article aims to make a valuable contribution to the transformation process in the energy sector by examining green energy, sustainability goals, and how blockchain technology can be integrated into sustainability studies in the green energy sector and the studies carried out in this direction.

articleTitle: Modeling and Designing Supply Chain Network Under Demand Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper aims to present an integrated research framework that provides an approach for making resilient decisions under deep uncertainty, especially in the supply chain. This paper develops a conceptual model using the unified modeling language technique, type activity diagrams (UML-Ads) which is a comprehensive modeling tool that helps con- conceptualize a configuration framework of supply chain management processes under demand uncertainty. The results show how the new approach contributes to understanding and managing load and capacity under demand disruption. Moreover, this paper explores some of the most complex variables that affect supply chain performance under high demand variation. It is possible to show the risk of obsolete materials and products clearly. The design science research methodology was chosen as a tool to generate strategic knowledge and model a new approach to make resilient decisions and solve a specific problem in the supply chain. This paper is original and contributes towards sharing a new approach helping to understand the supply chain within an uncertain context.

articleTitle: A Review of Advancements in Driver Emotion Detection: Deep Learning Approaches and Dataset Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This review paper delves into the rapidly evolving field of driver emotion detection, with a specific focus on the contributions of deep learning methodologies and the diverse datasets that facilitate this research. Facial emotion detection and recognition is a highly dynamic and challenging field in Machine Learning (ML) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). It has gained attraction for several decades, but it is extremely challenging due to the intrinsic complexities associated with understanding and interpreting human emotions. Understanding and responding to a driver's emotions is increasingly important when autonomous or assisted driving becomes common. To ensure safety, comfort, and optimal interaction between the driver and the car's systems, predicting the emotional state of the driver is essential, also of great significance in practical applications. We give a comprehensive survey of the state-of-the-art driver emotion recognition works that can effectively make use of the recent deep-learning approaches to identify complex emotional cues. Moreover, we explain a variety of datasets that play a vital role in flourishing this field along with the analysis of their effect, like AffectNet, CK+, and EMOTIC. Via this survey we try to investigate the challenges authors are faced with involving this field, e.g., concerns about data privacy, real-time processing demands, and the need for interdisciplinary collaboration. More importantly, the potential of these technologies to improve the driving experience and road safety has been highlighted. We hope this survey can benefit researchers and practitioners to have more insights and provide directions for advancing drivers’ emotions.

articleTitle: Blockchain-IIoT Integration: Revolutionizing Smart Manufacturing Process Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: This paper examines the integration of Blockchain and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) in manufacturing process monitoring. The proposed model emphasizes Blockchain's decentralization, cryptographic security, and smart contracts for enhanced security and efficiency. It addresses challenges like data security and scalability, showcasing the transformative potential of Blockchain-IIoT integration. In the end this work highlights future development opportunities in smart manufacturing.

articleTitle: Security and Privacy-Preserving Techniques of Federated Learning in Edge Computing: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Edge Computing (EC) is an innovative architecture that aims to provide cloud computing services near data sources. In conventional deep learning systems that use edge computing, data producers frequently need to transmit and exchange data with other entities, such as edge or cloud servers, to train their models. Federated Learning (FL) has recently emerged as a potential remedy for the problems of undesired bandwidth use, data confidentiality, and legal compliance. To enhance the status of research in this field and effectively implement the federated learning strategy, it is essential to identify and analyze its security and privacy issues first. Federated learning (FL) is the optimal method for addressing security and privacy concerns in edge computing. A profound grasp of risk factors allows FL implementers to create a secure environment while researchers benefit from a clear understanding of prospective research areas. The primary objective of this study is to evaluate previous contemporary studies in relevant disciplines to understand the issues and subjects covered in recent surveys. Furthermore, FL research is categorized into architectures, applications, and issues. Moreover, we analyze substantial security and privacy risks and propose new mitigation strategies.

articleTitle: Understanding Energy Consumption behavior by Analyzing Security Impacts and Mitigation Strategies in a Critical Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) play a pivotal role in critical applications, ranging from industrial control systems to healthcare monitoring. As these networks become increasingly integrated into our daily lives, understanding their energy consumption behavior is paramount for achieving sustainability and resilience. This paper delves into the intricate relationship between energy consumption patterns in WSNs and their security implications within critical contexts. We commence by conducting a comprehensive analysis of energy consumption behavior in WSNs, considering factors such as data transmission, node mobility, and sensing activities. Through empirical studies and simulations, we identify key parameters influencing energy utilization and establish a foundation for further investigation. Building upon this understanding, we explore the security impacts associated with the energy profile of WSNs operating in critical environments. We address potential vulnerabilities arising from compromised nodes due to energy depletion, communication constraints, and malicious attacks. By examining these security challenges, we highlight the urgency of developing robust solutions to ensure the reliability and integrity of WSNs in critical applications. In response to these challenges, we propose mitigation strategies that synergistically address both energy consumption and security concerns. Our approach based on security information and event management with deep learning security use case algorithms for impact mitigation. These strategies aim to enhance the overall sustainability and security of WSNs, ensuring their continued functionality in demanding and sensitive environments. In conclusion, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the intricate interplay between energy consumption behavior and security impacts in WSNs within critical contexts. Our findings underscore the need for holistic approaches that integrate energy-awareness and security measures to fortify the resilience of WSNs, fostering their sustainable deployment in critical applications.

articleTitle: Hydraulic Profile of Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants: Bibliographic Synthesis and Innovative Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: The calculation of the hydraulic profile for wastewater treatment plants requires a meticulous approach to hydraulic calibration to address operational issues related to overflows and hydraulic turbulence. Three hydraulic design approaches for Water Treatment Plants (WTP) and Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTP) have been identified, involving the establishment of hydraulic profiles after the selection of the flow diagram, the calculation of the hydraulic profile at the beginning of the design, and the progressive establishment of the profile during the sizing of structures. Despite the complexity of flow in wastewater treatment plants, hydraulic calculations are carried out for various flow scenarios, including average, peak during rainy weather, and minimum flows. The calculation of the hydraulic profile, conducted from the downstream control point to the upstream, may vary based on the designers' approach, underscoring the need for constant verification. Currently, no comprehensive hydraulic model for the calibration of STEP treatment plants has been published, emphasizing the significance of this work that presents different existing models with their specific constraints.

articleTitle: Electric Motor Control Methods and Improvements Applied to Electric Vehicles: A State of the Art
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: As a result of energy-related worries concerning energy shortage and global warming, investigations are conducted so as to provide solutions to integrate renewable energy and to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases caused especially by transportation.
